docs/platform/git/spec.md.title: 4. Publication port: refs/fgos/*
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sample: 4. Publication port: refs/fgos/*
docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 4. Publication port: refs/fgos/*
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 4. Publication port: refs/fgos/*

Event Store's crate-internal driver (event-store spec §3/§20) moves behind this port **without a protocol change**. Node reaches publication through the **combined N-API addon** (below) with **no exception** to the exec guard under the `state` lock. Git is forbidden under state 60. Event Store bounded append/read inside state remains its own in-process/open-log path; no DAG walk or Git call there.

**One Node load: one combined addon (owner decision Q1, topology (a)).** A Node process reaches exactly one in-process instance of `fgos-git`. Two independent Rust cdylib addons cannot share one in-process crate instance, so the Node payload ships **one combined N-API addon** that links both `fgos-event-store` and `fgos-git` and exports both facades. Event Store's seal/sync publication and every Node-reachable Git operation run through that one load. There is no per-operation host-process route (`fgos internal git <op>`) for Git and no JS-bridged second addon; topologies (b) and (c) are not adopted. A second, separate addon load of either crate in the same Node process fails closed, and doctor reports one ABI row for the combined addon. This changes Event Store's packaging (event-store spec §17, §21: its own addon of `fgos-event-store` becomes the combined addon); the signing bundle (2026-10-18) made that amendment, with the Publication port placement in event-store §3, §4 and §20. Rust consumers (observe, `fgos-work-state`) link `fgos-git` in-process. Reversal trigger: if experiment E3 shows the combined addon fails a budget stated before the run, or fails rollback with live processes (P-RELEASE), Q1 reopens.

Operations: writeBlob(bytes), writeTree(literal entries/modes/OIDs), writeCommit(tree, ordered parents, identity/message), readRef/Object, walkCommits(tips,cursor,bounds), compareAndSwap(ref,expected,next,operationId), fetchRefs and pushRefs. No index, worktree, HEAD, main-checkout lock, or consumer semantics.

**C1 — distinct execution policy.** Publication operates on direct namespace-qualified refs. It refuses symbolic refs in owned and mirror namespaces, validates the destination, and uses a backend mode that cannot follow a symbolic ref outside the grant even if the ref changes after preflight. A plain textual prefix check is insufficient. On the Git floor measured (2.53.0) a plain `update-ref` on a symbolic `refs/fgos/*` ref wrote through to `refs/heads/victim`, and `--no-deref` kept the victim unchanged but silently replaced the symbolic ref with a direct one while the expected-old check passed against the dereferenced value. Two separate checks therefore apply: (1) containment, the guarantee: every ref mutation runs in no-dereference mode with the expected OID on the actual update, so it never changes a ref outside `refs/fgos/*` even when the ref turns symbolic after preflight (the P-SYM-HOOK re-check confirmed this on 2.53.0: every `refs/heads/*` ref unchanged across the attack window, while the control without `--no-deref` moved the victim); (2) refusal, best effort: the ref is read as a symbolic-or-direct fact at preflight and again at read-back, and a symbolic ref found at either point is refused or reported as `recovery-required` tamper evidence. Detection of a **transient** substitution is not guaranteed: the same re-check turned a direct ref symbolic between preflight and the CAS, the `--no-deref` CAS overwrote it with a direct ref at the candidate, and both reads saw a direct ref, so read-back cannot recover the overwritten symbolic state. A substitution that is still present at read-back is detected. No detection mechanism for the transient case is claimed until a proof names one. An expected-OID match is never evidence that the ref was direct. Object writes and reads do not enable replace-object or alternate-object authority from worker input, and every identity/type/tree/ancestry/publication read runs with replacement objects disabled (`--no-replace-objects` or its environment equivalent): scrubbing `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE` does not disable repository-owned `refs/replace/*`, which made `cat-file` return a different commit for the same OID in the floor proof. Worker-supplied alternate-object, replace-ref and shallow authority (`GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE`, `--reference`-style overrides, config injected through the scrubbed env context of G-001/G-183) is always refused. Repository-owned layout in the trusted common dir (`.git/objects/info/alternates`, shallow, promisor remotes) is a compatibility profile: until E5 establishes which of these configurations `fgos-git` supports, an operation that needs an object unavailable under that layout refuses by name rather than fetching implicitly, and the refusal names the layout feature. Raw Git does not do this by itself: a read of a missing blob in a promisor partial clone spawned a lazy `fetch`, and a missing alternate gave a generic exit 128. So the hardened context sets no-lazy-fetch (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` on the measured floor) for every non-Remote operation (status, diff, read, checkout, merge, not only readObject); shallow, alternates and promisor layout are detected before invocation; a missing object or incomplete traversal becomes a named layout refusal that keeps the actual Git error. Any fetch or deepen is a Remote operation with its own authorization, never an Inspect repair.

Publication's private Git calls **cannot execute repository hooks**, including the **reference-transaction** hook, nor inherit worker-provided external commands. “No hook-running commit porcelain” is not enough: plain `update-ref` ran `reference-transaction` (`prepared`, `committed`) on the measured floor. Every Publication call carries a trusted hook-disabled configuration (`core.hooksPath` set by the backend to an fgOS-owned empty location; `/dev/null` suppressed the hook on 2.53.0) that no repository or worker config can override. This does not disable guards on ScopedCommit or checkout mutations. Transport helpers and credential providers are Remote capabilities, not implicit privileges of writeBlob/readObject/CAS.

Use explicit trusted common-dir plumbing. Validate object types and refs. Event Store provides the seal/merge manifests and parent order; Git never computes event union or business conflict outcomes.

Namespace grants are explicit: own events/local-events/branch-events and authorized one-time legacy import; mirrors only fetch-written; Git operation pins reserved to Git. CAS distinguishes absent from exact OID and returns actual tip on loss. No event segment deletion follows a Git receipt alone: Event Store still verifies coverage and durably records its own sealed receipt.

Required unchanged Event Store protocol:

1. Seal/sync owns event-seal 58; event-append 70 protects rotation only and is released before Git.
2. Write trees/commits, journal intent, CAS `refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>`; retain segments on CAS loss. Event Store retries by its section 10 rules.
3. Walk both parents of a DAG with visited set and bounded continuation. Only Event Store decides certified coverage pruning. Incomplete traversal never claims complete coverage.
4. Fetch `+refs/fgos/events/*:refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/events/*` and the existing legacy mirror mapping. `+` is allowed only for mirror refresh as Event Store §14 requires. Never overwrite own ref by fetch.
5. Push only own events and authorized legacy ref; never force-push, mirrors, local/branch streams or Git pins. Non-FF triggers Event Store fetch/reconcile using a two-parent commit then ordinary push. No Git-side event reconciliation.

**CAS and pin ordering (V-CAS fold).** A multi-ref `update-ref --stdin` transaction is **not** crash-atomic on the `files` backend: the Git floor proof killed one after the target rename and left target = next, pin = expected and `pin.lock` on disk. Reftable was exercised only for completed transactions. So Git never relies on multi-ref atomicity: the operation pin is written by exact-old CAS and read back as a prepare substep, the prepared WAL record is made durable, the TargetAttempt record of §10 is made durable, and only then is the target moved by a single-ref exact-old CAS. This order is mandatory and has no optimization: Git never puts a target publication in a multi-ref transaction, with the pin or with anything else (the M1 and V-CAS re-checks showed that combining the first pin install with the target publishes before a read-back pin and a durable prepared record). Recovery still admits every observed subset of a multi-ref transaction's effects and any retained native ref lock, because legacy writers and raw Git leave such residue; that admission never authorizes Git to write one. The pin is reachability against GC, not the receipt. The file WAL record remains the authority for intent, phase and attribution, and recovery reconciles target and pin from it (§10).

**Non-publication Node→Rust route** (commit-scoped, land, worktree): the same combined addon, used **outside** state 60, never an exec-guard exception (owner decision Q1). Lock-taking operations through it use LockScope option (a) of §5. Panelist 2's host route is not shipped; E3 measures the chosen route against the current Node writers and is the reversal trigger named above.

Phase 02 handoff note: the dormant Node Publication constructor currently acquires
its own event-seal synchronously. Phase 02 replaces this with the caller's held
seal External/borrow; the stored helper is not yet used for that handoff. A caller
already holding the same seal cannot use this constructor until that switch.

Reftable was exercised only for completed transactions. So Git never relies on multi-ref atomicity: the operation pin is written by exact-old CAS and read back as a prepare substep, the prepared WAL record is made durable, the TargetAttempt record of §10 is made durable, and only then is the target moved by a single-ref exact-old CAS. This order is mandatory and has no optimization: Git never puts a target publication in a multi-ref transaction, with the pin or with anything else (the M1 and V-CAS re-checks showed that combining the first pin install with the target publishes before a read-back pin and a durable prepared record). Recovery still admits every observed subset of a multi-ref transaction's effects and any retained native ref lock, because legacy writers and raw Git leave such residue; that admission never authorizes Git to write one. The pin is reachability against GC, not the receipt. The file WAL record remains the authority for intent, phase and attribution, and recovery reconciles target and pin from it (§10).

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 5. Layering and unchanged 4.3-R locks
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 5. Layering and unchanged 4.3-R locks

Reuse Holder-lock's registry, existing paths/ranks, kernel drivers, description borrowing, predecessor domain and fences **unchanged**. No TTL/heartbeat/PID-based authority, inode deletion/recreation or new lock map.

Every mutating request declares a canonical resource set and the **existing** authority required for that set. Normal execution and recovery acquire the same resource authority. Publication of an Event Store stream uses event-seal; branch land uses merge-slot and, where needed, worktree-admin/main-checkout; worktree effects require the applicable admin/main authority and continuous Execution custody. A supervisor recovery lock may serialize the supervisor; it **never** substitutes for these authorities and is not a repository-wide journal mutex. Recovery determines needed resources before acquiring locks. Unsupported or missing authority refuses mutation.

A fresh Rust scope must not hide the Node caller's held locks. Unknown mutation posture fails closed. Holder-lock §9 defines LockScope as a Node object that acquires kernel locks by spawning `fgos internal lock-fd` with the fd in stdio slot 3; it defines no cross-language handle, and none is added.

**LockScope option (a) (owner decision Q1).** For lock-taking operations (commit-scoped, sync, land, worktree, restore), Rust `fgos-git` acquires the ranks it needs (20/40/50) in its **own Rust LockScope**. The Node caller passes, as explicit parameters of the operation, the ranks its scope holds and a descriptor for each held lock the operation relies on (for example the `dispatch-cwd` lease that is the custody token). The Rust scope seeds its rank floor from those held ranks, so the Holder-lock rule "acquire only above every held rank" applies across the N-API boundary exactly as inside one Node scope. A passed descriptor is never trusted as declared: Git verifies it with the three-condition borrower test of holder-lock §5 (named lock, `fstat` `dev:ino` equal to the lock file, `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` on that description succeeds) before any effect and again before the irreversible boundary. A held-rank list without a verified descriptor confers no authority, and a set of rank numbers alone is never a lock (no bitmap). The borrower test proves only that the description is usable and exclusive **at the moment of the test**: the model-check probe opened a free lock file, matched name and inode, and `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` succeeded because it had just acquired the lock (holder-lock §19 names this case). So a descriptor is accepted only as an acquired handle of the caller's Holder-lock scope in the same process, passed through the combined addon as an opaque handle, never as an fd number or path taken from request input; handles are close-only, a revoked or closed handle is refused, and a successful try-lock never proves continuous custody or a generation handoff (§6). Git children receive a verified lease only through `run_borrowed`. Rust-acquired locks are released by closing their descriptions before the operation returns, so the Node scope never sees a lock it did not take. Publication is unaffected: under seal 58 it never acquires 20/40/50.

| Rank | Resource / rule |
|---|---|
| 20 | Existing per-target merge-slot; reserve before expensive land work; no-wait handled here |
| 30 | Existing `dispatch-cwd` lease, held by Execution and extended across the runner commit; the custody token Git validates. **Not** a Git lock and never acquired by Git. See N7. |
| 40 | Existing worktree-admin. Holder-lock §16 (amended 2026-10-17, owner decision Q6) wraps add, remove, relocate (move) and prune. Because it serializes worktree registration, Git also holds it across the checkout revalidation, CAS and read-back of every Refs mutation of `refs/heads/*` (§3) and of Land publication (§9 step 4); holder-lock §16 leaves to this section which Git operations take it. |
| 50 | Existing main-checkout, only short actual main index/tree/HEAD mutation/recovery |
| 55 | Git-native index.lock, never an fgOS implementation |
| 58 | Event Store event-seal; publication cannot acquire 20/40/50 beneath it |
| 60 | Consumer state; no Git, child, verify/build or lower-rank acquisition |
| 70 | Event Store event-append; no Git while held |
| 80 | Existing leaves such as recovery, only after all needed lower ranks; release before later state 60 settlement |

The common order remains 20→40→50→60. Operations take only needed locks. Verify/build never runs under 50/60. Publish revalidates under appropriate locks and performs no arbitrary Node callback. Consumer settlement follows release. Recovery requiring main takes 20/40/50 before recovery 80; publication recovery without checkout takes no main/admin and remains compatible with caller seal 58. No invented publication lock rank.

**worktree-admin wrap set (owner decision Q6).** G-042 and G-155 require dirty-check through destroy under one ownership. Holder-lock §16 is amended (2026-10-17) so that `worktree-admin` (rank 40) wraps add, remove, relocate (move) and prune: the dirty-check, the destroy or move, and the registration change run under one hold of 40. It is still one lock; Git callers **must not invent a second admin lock**. The amendment's implementation lands with the Git component. Read-only listing is not a globally serialized exclusive operation and takes no lock.

**Rank-30 versus rank-20 legality (R30; owner-decided structure; M2 held in the model abstraction, §19).** Rank 30 is the `dispatch-cwd` lease (holder-lock §7), taken by a dispatch on its worktree in the runner's per-dispatch LockScope above `runner` 10 and, once it exists, `attempt` 15. Under Q2 it is held from producer start through the runner commit and handoff; under Q1 the Rust scope inherits the caller's held ranks, so the Holder-lock rule "acquire only above every held rank" binds Git exactly as it binds the Node scope. Every rank below is an existing registry row; the table invents none.

Execution rejects a mutating Unit that resolves to the main checkout before opening a native Git port or acquiring/borrowing custody; this policy refusal takes precedence over Git lock-admission errors. Resume reports a live cwd holder through the same coded `dispatch-in-flight` refusal as dispatch. A controller crash after native commit return leaves the real persisted ScopedCommit intent pending; resume recovers that intent and settles the original receipt without launching the producer or committing again. Runner regressions: `test/runner/execution/run.test.mjs` and `run-resume-order.test.mjs`.

| Operation | Locks Git acquires (in order) | May already be held by the caller | Illegal combination and how the protocol avoids it |
|---|---|---|---|
| ScopedCommit in a linked worktree (runner commit) | none; Git's own `index.lock` 55 inside the git child | 10, 15, 30 (required: verified `dispatch-cwd` lease on that worktree, borrowed into the git children) | Missing or stale 30 fails closed. Git never acquires 20 or 40 here, so holding 30 is never an inversion. |
| ScopedCommit or checkpoint in the main checkout | 50 | 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 | Holding 30 then taking 50 is legal. Holding 60 or 70 is illegal (rank rule; no Git under state). Holder-lock `run_borrowed` maps one description per child: a git child that must carry both a 30 lease and 50 needs a second mapped slot, which Holder-lock does not define; until Holder-lock is amended for that, the combination is refused and the runner commit runs in a linked worktree only. |
| Sync start/continue/abort (producer worktree, pinned target OID) | none (target is pinned by OID, so no 20) | 10, 15, 30 (required) | Sync never takes 20: catchup reads and pins the target tip and does not publish it. Missing or stale 30 fails closed. |
| Land prepare/publish (merge or squash into a target ref) | 20, then 40 for candidate create, release 40, then 40 and 50 for publication | 10, 15 only | **Land needing 20 while holding 30 is an inversion.** The protocol avoids it: land never runs inside a dispatch scope. The runner commit and handoff end, the `dispatch-cwd` lease is released, and land is entered from a scope that holds no rank above 15 (the runner's merge path or a merge verb). A land request whose held ranks include 30 or anything above 20 is refused with `lock-order-violation` before any effect. Land does not need the producer's 30: it works in its own detached candidate worktree. |
| Worktree create / createDetached | 40, unless the caller lends its own verified worktree-admin of this repository (2026-10-20, phase 07: the waiting `addWorktree` door holds it; nothing above 40 may be held with it) | 10, 15, 20, 30 (when the caller holds another worktree's lease), 40 (lent, as stated) | Taken below 50, never while 50 or 60 is held. The new worktree's own 30 does not exist yet (its key is `dev:ino` of the new directory); Execution takes it after create returns, outside every Git lock. |
| Worktree remove / relocate (move) | 40, unless lent as for create | 10, 15, 20, 30 (required when the worktree has a live custody holder: the caller's verified lease on that worktree), 40 (lent) | 30 then 40 is legal. Removing or moving a worktree whose 30 is held by another holder is refused, never forced. |
| Worktree prune / repairRegistration | 40, unless lent as for create | 10, 15, 20, 40 (lent) | Prune never acquires 30. Prune acts only on registrations whose directory is missing; a directory that exists is handled by remove under the rule above. |
| SafeRestore (producer worktree) | none | 10, 15, 30 (required) | Missing or stale 30 fails closed. |
| SafeRestore (main checkout) | 50 | 10, 15, 20, 40 | Holding 60 or 70 is illegal. |
| Refs ensureBranch/advanceRef/deleteRef/fastForwardCheckedOut on `refs/heads/*` (changed by the 2026-10-18 re-check fold; was "none") | 40, held from the checkout revalidation through the exact-old CAS and read-back | 10, 15, 20, 30 (fastForwardCheckedOut requires the verified 30 on the one worktree that holds the branch) | Holding 40, 50, 60 or 70 is refused with `lock-order-violation` before any effect, so 40 is never taken under main 50 (order 20→40→50). Only Worktree borrows a lent 40; Refs, Land and Remote always take their own. Exact-old CAS serializes the ref value; 40 serializes checkout membership, which the CAS does not see. A branch checked out in any worktree is refused (§3) except under fastForwardCheckedOut. Post-land branch cleanup runs after land, outside the dispatch scope. Refs on `refs/fgos/*` are Publication (row below), never checked out, and take no lock. |
| Publication (Event Store seal/sync, `refs/fgos/*`) | none (Event Store holds event-seal 58) | anything below 58 | Never 20/40/50 under 58; never under 60 or 70. |
| Remote fetch/push of non-event refs | none | anything below 60 | No Git under 60. |
| RepositoryConfig (fetch mapping and hooks) | repo-config 80 | anything below 60; recovery refuses caller loans | The resource authority serializes fgOS writers and ConfigChange recoverers; native config.lock excludes ordinary Git config writers. ConfigChange recovery takes no peer-rank recovery leaf. |
| Recovery of an interrupted operation | owning resource authority, then `recovery` 80 last; non-event transfer recovery uses 40 then 80; Publication uses only caller event-seal 58; ConfigChange uses only repo-config 80 | as for that operation; non-event transfer recovery below 40; ConfigChange no caller loans | Recovery 80 never replaces resource authority and is released before any later state 60 settlement. |

The table is the structure the owner chose (Q1 option (a), Q2 lease extension). M2 (unit-run-1792254306261-e7f3b8ba) enumerated every subset of the 11 ranks against 26 operation and recovery profiles and 5 descriptor states (266,240 cases) and found no two-scope wait cycle, including the refusal of a land request that carries 30. That is a check of the abstraction, not of fairness, bounded waiting, cancellation, alias identity or descendant drain, and the hook was encoded as a single probe; V-ORDER still has to exercise the real Node→addon→Rust→hook ladder. M2 ran with the Refs row taking no lock; its new rank-40 profile is legal by the rank rule (40 above every rank it may be held with) and is re-checked in §19.

Borrow via existing `run_borrowed` only: exact child fd mapping, CLOEXEC restored, inode/description try-lock borrower check, close-only release, gc/maintenance auto off, wait for child domain empty. Text env/PID grants do not confer authority. Hook strangers probe once and never wait while holding index 55. Activity beacon is advisory, never a lock.

Monotonic bounded wait budget covers retries. Retry only named contention, not lock-order/corruption/unknown protocol errors. Cancellation/timeout uses Process containment, not a process-group kill alone: in the Git floor proof a hook and a clean filter started a child that called `setsid()`, and that child survived `killpg` of the Git group both under a deadline and after Git exited 0. A group kill is a guarantee only for members that stay in the group. Descendant drain is claimed only where a Process containment domain whose driver answers `Empty` exists (process spec §4-5: `linux-gate`; Windows `job-object` per holder-lock §8.1); elsewhere, after the direct Git child exits or is killed, Git reports `containment-unproven` as `recovery-required` for that operation and its worktree, keeps the WAL evidence, and never infers that the domain is empty or that a successor may enter. Holder-lock's `run_borrowed` leftover kill (holder-lock §8: on Linux every process still holding the lock description, by identity) still runs; it covers escapees that kept the description, not those that closed it. Git installs no process-wide handler that kills Node. Post-effect cancellation records/reports pending recovery. Platform guarantee and macOS containment limits inherit Holder-lock; unsupported Windows/filesystem posture is a named failure until its driver is actually activated/proven.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 6. N7 and RUL84
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 6. N7 and RUL84

**N7 — ownership and mechanism decided (owner decision Q2).** Execution owns continuous custody from producer start through attempt exit, runner commit, receipt and handoff. Worker exit never releases custody. Git validates it and owns the mutation, not attempt scheduling. Successor producer/reset/sync/remove/commit is refused until current generation handoff is proven. Missing/stale custody fails closed. Read-only workflows require no writable custody.

**Mechanism: the existing `dispatch-cwd` lease, extended across the runner commit.** There is no new Custody entity (design principle 1). The lease Execution already takes on the worktree (rank 30, holder-lock §7, runner RUL101) is no longer released at the end of the assignment; it is held through the runner commit, its receipt and the handoff, and only then released. Contract:

- Execution passes the lease to Git as a held rank plus its descriptor (§5, LockScope option (a)). Git verifies the descriptor by the holder-lock §5 borrower test before any effect and again before the irreversible boundary; a missing, unverifiable or stale lease (wrong `dev:ino`, a description that no longer holds the lock, a worktree whose identity changed) fails closed with a named cause.
- Git children of the operation (commit, hooks) receive the lease through `run_borrowed`, like any other borrowed lock, so a dying Node caller does not free the worktree while git still writes in it.
- Git never acquires, extends or releases the lease; Execution does.
- The change to the run supervisor and to the lease lifetime (closing the gap named in holder-lock §19, "released before the runner commits the Unit's writes") is implementation work owned by the Git plan. This spec states the contract only and does not amend holder-lock §19.
- Predecessor-domain emptiness on Linux/macOS is **not** an existing guarantee (holder-lock §19); that assumption stays currently **false** until the attempt lock exists.

**Successor admission after controller death (M3 / P-CUSTODY fold).** The model check found the shortest violation in two steps, “controller dies → successor acquires free lease”, and reproduced it with a real kernel `flock`: a producer descendant that did not hold the lease description kept writing in the worktree while the successor held the lease. A git child that holds a borrowed description is excluded correctly; a producer process is not, because it holds no copy. So a free `dispatch-cwd` lease is **not** proof of generation handoff. Rule:

- Successor producer, reset, sync, remove or commit on a worktree may start only when the previous custody generation ended by a recorded handoff (lease closed by Execution after the receipt), **or** the previous holder's whole process domain is proven empty by the holder-lock §8 predecessor rule: the custody holder declares the producer's containment domain in the lease's predecessor record before the producer starts, and the successor, after it holds the lease, applies holder-lock §8 steps 2-3 unchanged (kill a non-empty domain at once, then proceed only when Process `domain_is_empty` answers `Empty`; otherwise `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)`). Execution applies this rule when it acquires the lease for a successor, because it owns custody (Q2); Git still only validates the lease it is handed.
- Where no domain was declared, or the domain kind has no driver that answers `Empty` (today: Linux and macOS until the attempt lock and run-supervisor containment exist; `macos-tree` answers `Unknown`; Linux without a PID namespace is best-effort), admission **fails closed** with `custody-predecessor-unknown`. It never assumes the domain is empty. The worktree and its bytes are preserved and reported by `git-worktree-recovery`; Execution may dispatch the successor in a **new** worktree, so a refused worktree does not stop the item.
- The producer itself never receives the lease description: any copy may `LOCK_UN` (holder-lock §5 rule 6), and a descendant that closes its fds escapes anyway. Inheriting the fd is therefore not the safety mechanism; the domain proof is. Handing the lease to the attempt gate, which runs inside the domain, is the holder-lock §6 lease form and is how the domain proof and the lease coincide once the gate exists.

- **Recorded handoff over a best-effort domain (owner decision 2026-10-19).** After a successful run Execution clears its own predecessor record once the producer's domain is observed empty (holder-lock §8 step 0). For `linux-pgroup` and `macos-tree` that observation cannot see a `setsid` or double-fork escapee, so the handoff does not cover one; on supervised Linux the attempt gate (a subreaper) kills such escapees before the receipt. Refusing to clear best-effort records was rejected: it would strand the worktree after every unconfined Linux or macOS run.

No claim of concurrent commit safety until the lease extension and this admission rule are implemented and V-CUSTODY passes on the implementation. The M3/P-CUSTODY re-check (§19) held only in a finite model and a fixture probe: the old witness is now refused with `custody-predecessor-unknown`.

**RUL84.** The lowest shared **write-scope foundation leaf** owns the grammar/matcher/expansion; Execution owns granted paths; Git enforces them. One Rust implementation and one port; no Node matcher plus a Rust copy. It may initially be a leaf module of the Git package but imports no operations or consumer. Replace `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` with a thin facade in the same switch, preserving exports/golden semantics. Packaging (leaf vs independent crate) follows the route decision; it does not give Git ownership of Execution's grant policy.

Preserve grammar: canonicalize declaration trim/dot/separators/consecutive whole `**`; reject absolute/`..`/backslash/NUL/leading colon/embedded `**`. Only `*` within segment and whole-segment `**` glob; all other metacharacters literal; plain entries cover subtree by full segments. Query path bytes are not trimmed; both rename ends are checked. `.fgos` is excluded even by `**`. Generated grants use the same expansion primitive. Byte paths not representable by existing string grammar are refused with lossless encoded path, never lossy-matched.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.sample: 7. Hardened Git backend, parsers and hook contract
docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 7. Hardened Git backend, parsers and hook contract
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 7. Hardened Git backend, parsers and hook contract

2026-10-19 (operation preflight): each ScopedCommit/Sync port call (including preflight, recovery, checkpoint and abort) reads effective repository config and object/ref formats once through the existing driver, validates config trust and format compatibility, and keeps those facts only on an internal handle owned by that call. The long-lived port handle stores no config snapshot. Hook-path selection uses the same effective records. Disk topology/reciprocal registration and custody are still checked before every child. After every hook-bearing command, including rejection or transport failure, the driver invalidates the facts and reads/checks them once again before observation or cleanup. A failed refresh fences all subsequent Git commands in that call; the next call starts fresh. Raw external Git remains outside cooperative exclusion. Publication and checkout share one ConfigStamp validation door: before each child, stat cached global/system paths, common config, worktree config and origin files; a stamp mismatch re-reads and rechecks effective config before proceeding. A change during that read refuses the operation. Post-hook refresh also compares promisor status and refuses a change, as it does for object/ref formats. Publication CAS behavior is unchanged.

One private CLI driver; no shell interpolation. Runner policy scrubs inherited `GIT_*` and constructs explicit typed per-call overrides. Preserve currently supported author/committer identity/date and trusted config-file policy; worker-controlled config env is not trusted input. Disable fsmonitor; merge rerere and autoStash off; borrowed automatic gc/maintenance off. Per-child overrides disable signature display, decoration, abbreviated commit display and color so formatted log/show/rev-list reads remain machine-readable regardless of user display configuration. Gitdir authority comes from trusted common-dir registered backlink and real path/identity, never worker `.git`. Revalidate symlink/inode substitution before effect.

**Two named env contexts, one backend owner (C6 / G-001 vs G-183):** (1) scrubbed runner calls; (2) validated hook context that retains Git-supplied index/worktree/gitdir so guards inspect exactly the commit index (including temporary index). Never scrub that authority away. Worker cannot request hook context by arbitrary env bag. Resolve hooksPath relative to trusted main; setup writes absolute owned path when filling an empty slot, preserves custom hook path and diagnoses missing enforcement.

No hardcoded trunk: explicit consumer target, remote default, then validated main attached branch; ambiguity/missing target is named. Full refs/end-of-options prevent tags/options/ranges from changing meaning. Validate commit type. Batch object/path-at-revision returns error distinct from absence.

NUL-delimited lists everywhere including worktree list; literal paths/no trim; status explicit untracked; diff `--no-relative`; scope lists `--no-renames` or return both ends. Stage literal NUL pathspec stdin, never glob argv. Stream outputs or preserve explicit equivalent ceilings (64MiB path lists, 50MiB review diff; blob guards stream); overflow is typed refusal, never silently incomplete.

Hook ordering (surviving guards; PID-grant and event-monotonicity steps **superseded**): stale-index guard; tracked `.fgos` deletion (non-event; event-file deletion only in authorized cutover grant); worker `.fgos` exclusion; root-file guard; warning-only convention; at-home check; main branch restriction; 4.3-R borrower/stranger probe; identity/beacon; beacon written last. Remove only the retired event monotonicity guard at Event Store cutover. Merge skips root allowlist exception only, not safety guards. Identity/index/blob/unknown-protocol failures close; corrupt advisory beacon warns. Physical trusted hook home and platform path equivalence are tested. Hook diagnostics retain underlying reason. Custom hook directory lacking mandatory guards is an explicit doctor gap.

**Event-file cutover grant (P-CUTOVER fold).** Today `.githooks/pre-commit` refuses every staged deletion under `.fgos/`, while Event Store §18 step 5 needs exactly one commit on main that deletes the tracked event files, `state.json` and the two backups. The grant for that one commit is a ScopedCommit whose intent carries `cutoverGrant {exactPaths, legacyRefOid, sealDigest}`, run under main-checkout 50. The hook recognizes it only when (1) it is the borrower of main 50 by the holder-lock §5 test and (2) the common-dir WAL holds a durable ScopedCommit intent of this operation whose `exactPaths` equal the staged deletions under `.fgos/` byte for byte, and whose `legacyRefOid` equals the current `refs/fgos/legacy`. No env variable, PID literal or `--no-verify` grants it. Every other `.fgos` deletion stays refused, including in that commit. The hook's support for the grant lands with the Event Store cutover change or earlier, whichever comes first, and is the same rule in both cases.

The grant also requires a durable TargetAttempt with no outcome (one shot), the SHA-256 digest of the legacy commit's `seal.json` to equal `sealDigest`, and includes the consumer-created `.fgos/events` fence when it changes. An already tracked unchanged fence is retained without forcing it into the staged delta; index-parent and repository gitdir comparisons use canonical paths.

**G-062 (owner amendment, 2026-10-20):** Git runs the commit hooks once. Preserve the original commit stderr verbatim, including whitespace and line endings; the result retains its bytes as well as its text. Failure of the commit alone does not prove pre-commit refusal. A diagnostic replay is permitted only for fgOS's owned guard: RepositoryConfig must prove the configured executable hook path's ownership/provenance. That is the identified **known safe guard invocation**; its failed replay is evidence for `hook-refused` / Unit `policy-refusal`. The diagnostic runs only through `git hook run pre-commit` in validated hook context (2), under the same custody. Its output never replaces the original commit evidence. A foreign hook is never replayed; return the generic hook-or-Git failure (`commit-rejected`, translated to Unit `git-error` / `execution-failure`) with original stderr. A post-hook config refusal also preserves that original stderr while fencing further Git calls. Git never spawns a hook file directly. `git hook run` requires the Git 2.36 release floor (E5).

2026-10-21 (phase 07 unit 25, host gate): a borrowed run (where commit hooks run) captures stderr up to 64 MiB, the ceiling holder-lock gives commit children; past it the operation is refused `borrow-output-limit: stderr`, never cut. Every other Git child keeps the 64 KiB stderr ceiling. The WAL records causes, never stderr.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: **Event-file cutover grant (P-CUTOVER fold).** Today `.githooks/pre-commit` refuses every staged deletion under `.fgos/`, while Event Store §18 step 5 needs exactly one commit on main that deletes the tracked event files, `state.json` and the two backups. The grant for that one commit is a ScopedCommit whose intent carries `cutoverGrant {exactPaths, legacyRefOid, sealDigest}`, run under main-checkout 50. The hook recognizes it only when (1) it is the borrower of main 50 by the holder-lock §5 test and (2) the common-dir WAL holds a durable ScopedCommit intent of this operation whose `exactPaths` equal the staged deletions under `.fgos/` byte for byte, and whose `legacyRefOid` equals the current `refs/fgos/legacy`. No env variable, PID literal or `--no-verify` grants it. Every other `.fgos` deletion stays refused, including in that commit. The hook's support for the grant lands with the Event Store cutover change or earlier, whichever comes first, and is the same rule in both cases.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: **G-062 (owner amendment, 2026-10-20):** Git runs the commit hooks once. Preserve the original commit stderr verbatim, including whitespace and line endings; the result retains its bytes as well as its text. Failure of the commit alone does not prove pre-commit refusal. A diagnostic replay is permitted only for fgOS's owned guard: RepositoryConfig must prove the configured executable hook path's ownership/provenance. That is the identified **known safe guard invocation**; its failed replay is evidence for `hook-refused` / Unit `policy-refusal`. The diagnostic runs only through `git hook run pre-commit` in validated hook context (2), under the same custody. Its output never replaces the original commit evidence. A foreign hook is never replayed; return the generic hook-or-Git failure (`commit-rejected`, translated to Unit `git-error` / `execution-failure`) with original stderr. A post-hook config refusal also preserves that original stderr while fencing further Git calls. Git never spawns a hook file directly. `git hook run` requires the Git 2.36 release floor (E5).

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ## 8. Scoped commit and sync
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 8. Scoped commit and sync

2026-10-20 (typed-operation performance): the existing storage-format probe batches object/ref formats in one Git invocation. ScopedCommit reuses its pre-staging dirty-path observation for the rollback inventory (no intervening worktree mutation), and reads the resulting immutable commit OID/tree/parents together. Land checkout enumeration reuses stamp-validated facts only when gitdir, common-dir and worktree all match through the same checkout-identity predicate; other worktrees still resolve their own config. Recovery’s old-index digest and expected next-index entries derive from the same canonical stage-entry read. These facts never persist beyond the operation; post-hook refresh, per-child topology/config/authority validation, WAL barriers and all exact-old/recovery guards remain required. The existing E3 `scoped-census` mode traces paired typed/legacy operations, listing Git exec arguments and exclusive holder-lock acquisitions separately from borrow validations; prepare and publish times are reported separately. The suite uses `scoped-census --observer wrapper` to count direct Git launches without an external tracing tool; it does not measure internal Git children or locks. The default host census requires strace and fails if tracing is unavailable. Census timings under strace are diagnostic, not E3 verdicts.

**Literal selected paths.** Scope declarations keep the RUL84 grammar, but a selected filename is a literal path, not another declaration. Star, tab, newline and surrounding whitespace round-trip as escaped UTF-8 JSON strings in the ScopedCommit WAL `paths` array. Staging uses `--literal-pathspecs` and NUL-terminated stdin. Invalid UTF-8 is refused with the existing lossless encoded diagnostic; NUL, absolute paths and traversal segments are refused. Resolver grants still require a path the declaration grammar can name exactly.

**Store exclusion and legacy event authority.** ScopedCommit omits `.fgos` and its descendants even under `**`, tracked or untracked, without refusing the other selected paths. Only explicit `legacyEvents.exactPaths` (the closed legacy event layout) or the existing cutover grant admits store paths. Every legacy event commit, including additions and modifications, validates main-checkout 50 borrowing through the same request validation as Checkpoint; the deletion hook checks the same closed layout and main-50 authority. Unknown recovery operation ids are typed errors; only a persisted pending intent can be abandoned before attempt.

**Unit record and continuation.** Execution persists the native pre-producer baseline and original writer identity, Sync operation id before start, and the exact pending ScopedCommit request before commit. Resume carries current verified custody into native inspection/recovery and reuses that recorded intent; it never manufactures a new pre-producer baseline. A writing attempt without one requires a new run. A known rejected Sync commit may be retried only through `Sync.continue` with a persisted fresh `nextOperationId`: Git carries the existing merge's recorded state into that new WAL operation, retaining the original terminal cause and resolver bytes. Preparation interruptions resume the same id/pin; unknown commit effects are observed, never replayed. Manual completion/abort settles and compacts the old Sync chain; completion is reported as outside rather than attributed to Git. The Unit adapter requests the existing Sync abort for a rejected **clean-start** merge before returning refusal; rejection while concluding a conflicted merge keeps it open. The baseline head advances only from the native Sync receipt/inspection, leaving its pre-existing dirty-path exclusions intact.

Before producer, check trusted linked worktree/custody, no foreign staged entries even in scope, no foreign MERGE_HEAD; capture source baseline, existing dirty paths/content and ref. Worker may not stage or commit. After producer, exact authorized path selection includes both rename sides/deletions; revalidate authority/state and stage only selected literal paths. On failure unstage only this operation's entries and preserve bytes/foreign changes/cause. No-op differs from failure. Verify actual committed set/tree after hooks. If hook changed it, return `committed-but-contract-violation` with real OID; preserve effect, do not retry producer as though nothing happened. Resume commit-only retains captured intent/custody.

Sync merges pinned target OID into producer using no-commit/no-ff. `prepare` leaves a clean owned merge in `prepared` state under continuous source custody so Work can verify before `continue` commits it, or `abort` restores it after a red check. Same-id preparation observes the existing operation and never commits it. `start` retains its existing immediate clean-commit contract for Unit sync. Source-side non-event tracked `.fgos` stays source-side; workers receive no store grants. Clean sync records two exact parents.

2026-10-20 (phase 07 unit 13): `Sync.prepare` accepts the consumer's literal `files` declarations with the same validation and application as Land's (§9): they replace the store restore for their own paths, are written and staged after the merge, are part of the request digest (a same-id request with other declarations is `operation-id-reused`), and abort restores them like every other staged merge path. `start` (Unit sync) declares nothing, so source-side `.fgos` stays source-side there. Catchup (`performCatchUp`) is Work's consumer: it reads the read-only `merge-tree` of the pinned target and the branch, reports a conflict outside `.fgos` as the verb's `conflict` before any checkout or Sync exists (so no merge bytes remain for Worktree removal to preserve), and declares the store rule Land uses (§9 unit 11) — `merge=union` `.fgos` conflicts and stale `.fgos` paths keep the target's bytes — plus the merge result's bytes for every other `.fgos` path the merge changes, so a catchup merge commit never reads as the branch reverting the target's store. A branch's own store write is left on the branch for Land to refuse as `fgos-write-rejected`. A merge Git refuses outright (G-067) returns Git's own refusal text as the reason.

**G-071 effective (C6), not A's “abort all out-of-scope”.** Only the operation's scopable conflicts receive a **temporary** resolver grant; original producer `writeScope` remains unchanged; non-event `.fgos`, unscopable and forbidden paths do not gain grants. Continue refuses leftover conflict markers (seven or more `<`, `>` or vertical-bar characters followed by whitespace/end; skip binary/non-regular files) without staging, and validates parents/MERGE_HEAD/index/custody, detects manual completion/abort as done/not-started/lost, stages only owned conflict paths. Hook rejection retains cause. Sync-only without conflict work never spawns a producer.

**G-202 frozen by owner decision Q5 (2026-10-17).** Catalogue §7 Q16 recorded catchup-vs-sync as an open design decision; the owner closed it. Catchup uses the same isolated scoped resolver **when custody exists** (verified `dispatch-cwd` lease, §6); without custody it aborts only its own merge. Land candidate conflicts **abort**. A scoped resolver session without custody is forbidden (no resolver on a worktree the runner does not own). The decision came from the owner, not from the frozen catalogue.

2026-10-19 (phase 05 re-review): checkout resources include the worktree's realpath directory identity (dev, inode and birthtimeNs), using the exact custody lock path. A recreated directory at the same path never inherits the dead checkout's chains. Legacy path-only chains remain readable; a binding to a different custody lock is foreign. Admission closes foreign Intent/Prepared chains as `CommitRejected{foreign-checkout-abandoned}` and foreign TargetAttempt/SyncState/SyncCommitAttempt chains as `CommitRejected{foreign-checkout-effect-unknown}` (replay remains recovery-required). It preserves existing terminal causes, releases their pins and attempts ledger compaction without touching the current index or replaying effects. Only outcome-append errors block admission. After the outcome is durable, pin-release/compaction errors produce `checkout-compaction-deferred` warnings and admission retries cleanup next time. WorktreeRemove and WorktreeMove source resources also carry the existing directory custody key, so live checkout attempts exclude lifecycle changes; checkout admission refuses active Create/Remove/Move path resources, filtering by operation kind so legacy checkout chains still receive foreign classification. A foreign chain with a durable outcome cannot block the current checkout even if its compaction is deferred; its id cannot be replayed by the new checkout.

Under verified checkout custody, admission and inline pre-attempt failures close Intent/Prepared chains with `AbandonedBeforeAttempt`; recovery unstages their exact paths only when HEAD equals the baseline and the complete staged set equals those paths. `ScopedCommit.recover({operationId})` is observe-only: exact ordered parent(s) plus the intended tree prove a landed commit. For the newest checkout chain, exact parents plus the verbatim request message also prove it; a different tree records `contract_violation:true`. Admission excludes later cooperative checkout attempts while a chain is open; retained peer baselines are checked conservatively without using record age. Recovery uses one bounded `git log -g -n 1024` call on the recorded branch, stopping candidate processing at the baseline barrier after a candidate entry. It exhausts exact parent/tree matches before message-only matches. A candidate must be reachable from current HEAD; a reflog-only (ABA/reset-away) match keeps the chain open recovery-required and names its OID as evidence. SyncIntent records the symbolic branch; changed branches refuse unresolved SyncCommitAttempt recovery, and legacy records without a branch refuse with `sync-reference-unrecorded`. Without immutable commit proof, unchanged baseline HEAD, an absent native index lock and quiescent custody permit terminal `CommitRejected{commit-effect-unknown}` (Sync: `sync-commit-effect-unknown`); unstage is limited to the operation's paths. Other ambiguous states remain recovery-required. No attempt is replayed. Same-id replay returns the recorded cause, including unknown effects. New Sync refuses detached HEAD as `sync-detached-head-refused`. Compacted Sync replay matches the request digest using the recorded reference (or None for older receipts), independently of the live branch, and returns its recorded terminal state (`conflict-aborted`, `hook-rejected`, or the unknown cause), never a generic `not-started`.

An observed Sync hook rejection records `CommitRejected{hook-rejected}` and retains the open merge and pin until explicit abort. Abort restores recorded clean merged paths in both index and worktree to HEAD (including removal of target-only additions), preserving resolver bytes only on recorded conflict paths; if no conflict state was durably recorded, all merge paths return to HEAD. Foreign staged paths still refuse. Terminal checkout chains use Publication's WAL compaction ledger after pin release, compacting terminal chains immediately; compact receipts preserve id/request/authority bindings and reconstruct committed files from immutable commits. Baseline-dirty in-scope files changed by the producer remain excluded and are reported as `preExistingInScope`. Rollback captures bytes only for dirty, untracked, ignored or absent declared paths; clean tracked files restore from HEAD with their original permission metadata reapplied. Skip-worktree entries are excluded from the clean inventory. SyncState optionally retains pre-merge permission metadata for clean merged regular files; older states remain readable without it. Restore failures do not stop independent path restores; after all attempts they report `commit-worktree-restore-required`. Git's representation/configuration limits (including submodules and symlink emulation) remain outside an exact-content guarantee. Once an outcome is recorded, a failed compaction returns the actual receipt with `warnings: ["checkout-compaction-deferred: …"]`; the next checkout admission retries compaction. Recovery's outcome-only API likewise preserves the recorded outcome and retained WAL. Unsupported literal control/star paths refuse before staging or Intent.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
## 9. Land: candidate, verification, publication

2026-10-20 (phase 06 unit 1, dormant; **not release-ready**): Rust `prepare_land`/`publish_land`, addon `GitLand`, and Node `createGitLand` implement prepare, evidence binding, publication and M4 receipt replay. `prepare({operationId, request})` owns the encoded destination merge-slot 20 for the native session; callers pass only lower held ranks (an already held slot is refused as `land-slot-already-held`, anything above 20 as `lock-order-violation`, before effects). The candidate is created through Worktree's detached allocation/WAL door under 40. Construction and consumer verification retain only slot 20, following steps 2-3 below; 40/50/60 are absent during verification. `publish(evidence)` reacquires 40 then 50, validates all three commit pins/types, exact candidate HEAD/index/status, bound OIDs/tree digest and nonempty opaque consumer evidence, then records `land-verified → target-attempt → outcome`. The candidate status check covers HEAD, index and tracked files; untracked verification or setup output cannot enter the frozen tree and does not block publication, while a staged addition or tracked edit refuses as `land-candidate-dirty`. The tree digest is the canonical SHA-256 digest of the immutable tree OID. Consumer-declared file bytes are applied before the candidate is frozen, with literal staging and symlink traversal refusal. Git does not execute or certify verification commands.

The own-file clean gate combines literal committed paths with the canonical declared footprint; absent footprint is fail-safe, `.fgos` never counts, and status disables rename folding so both staged rename ends count. The existing Refs ignored/incoming collision check is shared with Land. A colliding ignored non-store path refuses before CAS; an ignored store collision preserves bytes by leaving checkout reconciliation pending. Successful dirty non-overlapping publication reports `checkout: pending` (checkout-lagging), never synced. The receipt has `operationId` and `consumerSettlement: notOwnedByGit`; successful same-id replay returns its established receipt even after external ref ABA. Receipt persistence releases the session slot as well as 40/50; `close()` releases an abandoned session without erasing evidence. An unresolved same-id attempt is refused without any re-effect. Production caller migration remains deferred to phase 07. The M4 Node contract fixture demonstrates the consumer's unique `(repoIdentity, operationId, settlementKind)` identity and query-before-retry rule; it is not evidence that Work/Event Store have adopted that mechanism.

2026-10-20 (phase 06 unit 2, dormant): the existing `GitLand`/`createGitLand` port adds `recover({operationId, consumerAcknowledgement?}, held?) → {receipt, warnings}` through Rust `recover_land`; no separate repair core or production caller is introduced. Recovery acquires destination 20, admin 40, main 50, validates quiescence, then takes recovery 80 last. An existing native session excludes it. Foreign writer/repository/binding, corrupt chains and absent objects fail closed. Before TargetAttempt, recovery records `abandonedBeforeAttempt`; after TargetAttempt it never reissues the target CAS, adopts reflog-only candidates or rolls back another writer. A missing receipt at the recorded candidate can be completed with `effectObservedOnly`, preserving that attribution in compacted replay. Prepared pin=old can be CAS-repaired to the recorded candidate after object/parent checks; unknown native ref/index locks remain untouched.

Before publication without an ignored store collision, `land-verified` records bounded per-path old/next fingerprints, the old index tree/file fingerprint and the expected next stage-entry digest (including unrelated staged changes), using the existing no-follow snapshot primitive. Recovery finishes an exactly captured old checkout under 50; it completes an already-next checkout after read-back, and reports unrelated dirt as pending. Mixed files, missing fingerprints, unreadable/unsupported path types, index drift and the interrupted `read-tree` shape with an unowned `index.lock` return `recovery-required`, preserving files/index/lock. This unit does not manufacture native-lock ownership from a matching ref or index tree; the owned dead-child quarantine machinery remains the native-repair unit's responsibility (§11). Native `read-tree` is one Git child. In addition to the production filesystem checkpoints, isolated Linux/x86_64 ptrace tests SIGKILL its actual descendants after native index-lock creation, main-file writing, index writing and index installation; the files-next/index-old/lock-present shapes preserve the exact native residue. A direct constructed-state regression also checks that unknown lock contents are never adopted.

2026-10-20 (unit 5 recovery fixes): exact-old index proof uses canonical `ls-files --stage -z` digest plus index tree and per-path fingerprints, tolerating stat refresh. LandVerified explicitly records ignored-store reconciliation skips. Unresolved recovery checks main native state, including `index.lock` and `MERGE_HEAD`, even when the destination is no longer checked out; terminal and compacted receipt replay precede that check. Prepare/publish check native main state only when the destination is checked out there. Post-attempt recovery rechecks writer equality against the chain inspected under destination slot 20.

2026-10-20 (phase 06 review fixes): two-tree reconciliation preserves staged modifications and staged additions outside the own-file set; staged overlap refuses before CAS. Recovery captures the expected next index stage-entry digest and can finish or recognize the same preserved staged state. Legacy proofs without next entries retain their clean-index expectation. WAL outcome `pendingStoreCollision` distinguishes an untouched checkout from reconciled checkout with tolerated dirt (`pending`); both map to receipt `Checkout::Pending`. Prepare validates declared file paths before allocating candidates; later failures retain the candidate path and Worktree operation id in bounded error diagnostics. Under the destination slot, admission closes the same writer/authority's pre-attempt Land chains as `abandonedBeforeAttempt`, retaining pins/candidate; a different writer requires named recovery. Finished same-id replay precedes slot acquisition, and lost replay retains the stale error and receipt. Publish checks WAL phase before live ref/candidate checks; an attempted identity requires recovery even when the ref moved. Refs and Land share post-attempt checkout-facts/CAS classification: unchanged or candidate tip after a failed native CAS requires recovery evidence, only a third-party tip is Loss. Already-merged source tips refuse a fresh Land identity.

2026-10-20 (phase 07 unit 11): Land never interprets `.fgos`, decision rows or merge attributes. Work computes its trusted-side resolutions before `prepare` from a read-only `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the exact source and target OIDs and passes them as declared `files`: a decision-id collision on the decision index (renamed decision file as a deletion plus new bytes, unioned index), a conflict confined to `merge=union` `.fgos` paths, and every `.fgos` path the branch did not write since its take point keep the target's bytes. Any other conflict is the verb's `conflict`; any remaining `.fgos` change is `fgos-write-rejected` before a candidate exists. Declarations are bound to the target they were read against, so only then is `target` passed; otherwise Land pins the destination itself. The repo-invariant checks run in the candidate with the item's verify.

2026-10-20 (phase 07 unit 12): every runner merge (root into the trunk, leaf into `fgw/<root>`, a nested root's sync into its parent, a promoted member into its integration branch) is one consumer sequence, `landRunnerItem` in `src/runner/merge.mjs`, on this Land transaction. The destination slot is only Land's, keyed by the full destination ref; the verbs' caller-held slot, the short-branch key, the ephemeral merge worktree with its own ref CAS and the main-checkout merge commit are deleted. The `MERGE_HEAD` refusal and the no-wait main precheck apply only when the destination is the branch the main checkout holds; a destination another linked checkout holds refuses as `foreign-target-checkout` (step 4) and the verb reports it as an error naming that target. Work event files a checkpoint is due for are committed by the temporary Work adapter's Checkpoint/ScopedCommit under main 50 before `prepare` pins the target; nothing is staged or swept around Land. An already-merged destination the main checkout does not hold is verified in a disposable detached checkout created through the Worktree admin door and removed through Worktree removal. After Work durably records the delivery (`approve`) or the sync decision (`sync-root`), the verb passes that record as `consumerAcknowledgement` to `recover`; a retained candidate is reported as a warning and never negates the land. Red, conflicted and promote candidates are still retained until a Work acknowledgement exists for them.

2026-10-20 (phase 07 unit 14): every `landRunnerItem` result whose operation Land journalled carries Work's settlement identity: `delivered` for a publication, `abandoned` for a result that published nothing (red verify, a candidate conflict, `main-checkout-dirty-mid-merge`, an unclassified failure). After Work durably records the result, the verb acknowledges it through the same `recover` door: approve's move to `blocked` (`work-blocked:<id>:<seq>`), an engine decision for a sync-root result that published nothing, and promote-to-component's one summary decision for every member, merged or not. Recovery closes the pre-attempt chain as `abandonedBeforeAttempt` and the existing cleanup admission removes its candidate, pins and journal. No identity is attached when Land journalled nothing under the id (a refusal before its intent), so there is nothing to release. A Land error that the verb rethrows (a lock refusal at publication) records no Work result and keeps its candidate.

2026-10-21 (phase 07 unit 24, review fixes): Recovery's `inspectOperation` refuses an id with no journal, live or compacted, with the exact cause `git-operation-unknown`. Approve records its Land operation id as a decision before Land starts; when a retry finds that decision and Land reports `git-operation-unknown` for it, no attempt exists under the id, so the retry reuses it (no second decision is written). Any other inspection failure still refuses. A recorded operation that is non-terminal at `land-verified` or `target-attempt` refuses the retry and names `fgos doctor --fix`, whose registered fix `git-land-recovery` lists pending operations through Recovery and reconciles each Land one through `recover_land` under its own locks: pre-attempt chains close `abandonedBeforeAttempt` whoever runs it (§10 rule 4b), attempted ones only from the writer that started them, and the fix names that writer otherwise; it releases no candidate, which stays until Work acknowledges it. In `landRunnerItem` an error in the publish phase that the consumer cannot classify records no Work result: the verb throws `land-effect-unknown` naming the same fix, and never claims an `abandoned` settlement for it. Post-land drift detection runs after the publication's error handling; its failure is reported in the result's `postLand.error` beside the land.

**Cleanup admission is precise:** no acknowledgement means retain candidate, all three pins and WAL, even after a successful receipt. A nonempty `consumerAcknowledgement` is the consumer's assertion that its unique `(repoIdentity, operationId, settlementKind)` entry is durably acknowledged; Git continues to return `consumerSettlement: notOwnedByGit` and never writes business settlement. Cleanup requires Worktree's existing clean, not-live and custody checks. Delivered candidates additionally require a reconciled/not-applicable terminal Land receipt and externally reachable delivery proof; terminal `abandonedBeforeAttempt` and `Loss` candidates require no delivered proof because nothing was delivered. The Worktree removal WAL binds the acknowledgement identity digest and caller writer before deletion. It uses the existing journaled Worktree removal door, then exact-old base/candidate pin deletes and the existing compact ledger. Dirty/unproven candidates, pending checkouts, changed pins and compaction failures are retained with warnings without negating Land. Compacted Land retains destination, expected/next, request/writer/authority binding and terminal attribution; same-id request replay returns the receipt after candidate deletion and external ref drift. An interrupted ledger deletion resumes under the same slot/admin authority. Land request matching uses a canonical digest of the declared request and writer, independent of disposable candidate directory identity.

Consumer supplies a source OID, an optional expected target OID, merge or squash, and **policy evidence bound to the prepared source/target/tree**. Omitting `request.target` pins the current destination only after Land acquires its own full-ref slot 20; an explicit expected target retains the exact-target stale check. The prepared candidate and persisted intent always contain the resulting target OID. `prepare({operationId, request, waitMs?})` waits only for slot admission (default zero); it never retries candidate construction or a publication CAS. `publish(evidence, {waitMs?})` likewise waits only for main-checkout 50 admission (default zero; merge verbs pass their existing `--wait` budget) and never retries the publication. In Node both waits are spaced single native attempts awaited on the event loop, never a blocking native wait: a blocked thread would also stop the verification children, timers and other Lands of that process, including a holder it waits for. An attempt that cannot take its lock has made no effect. Same-id replay matches the original declared request/writer digest, including whether an expected target was supplied, before taking the slot, even after cleanup/compaction or external destination movement.

Consumer `files` declarations may supply literal resolution bytes for candidate conflicts. Land proceeds only when every unmerged path has an exact declaration; otherwise it aborts the candidate and returns the existing conflict cause. It applies and stages these declarations before freezing the candidate commit/tree for verification. It never interprets decision rows or event meaning, and declarations for unrelated paths cannot authorize an uncovered conflict.

Work owns lineage/dependencies/approval/Iron Law; Git enforces the frozen binding and never imports Work. Workflow calls the same port. Squash creates a real one-parent commit; ordinary merge exact target/source parents; a staged squash index is not success.

Honest verification contract (not “nothing unverified is published” via tree equality):

- Consumer produces evidence bound to exact OIDs/tree (runs verify/build in the candidate worktree through Process, **outside Git**).
- Git binds that digest and refuses publish on mismatch, missing evidence, or dirty candidate (`write-tree` ≠ candidate commit tree, or digest mismatch).
- Git does **not** claim tests ran. A lying consumer can publish an unverified tree that matches the candidate. Tree proof is identity, not verification. V-VERIFY must not be marked passed by tree equality alone.

1. Reserve target merge-slot 20; inspect true topology, source/target and target checkout status/index/MERGE_HEAD. Reject foreign state.
2. Create detached operation candidate under admin 40, release admin, construct merge from pinned target. Land conflict aborts candidate only; source and target preserved. Consumer transformations of non-event `.fgos`/decision documents produce declared candidate bytes, not Git-owned state meaning.
3. Consumer verifies/builds outside 50/60. Freeze tree/evidence before and after; any changed candidate/dependency setup invalidates evidence. No post-verify strip/renumber can publish bytes that do not match the bound digest. Pin candidate/bases against normal GC.
4. Reacquire required admin 40/main 50 in order; revalidate target/source, evidence and candidate; re-run the own-file-set clean gate (G-098/G-102: union of committed diff and declared footprint, normalized; whole-repo scope for land, subtree scope for return; `.fgos` never counts; fail-safe to every non-`.fgos` path when the set is absent; a staged rename blocks when either half is own) and return `main-checkout-dirty-mid-merge` without moving the ref when it fails. Never use main dirty bytes as merge input. Detect foreign linked checkout holding target; v1 refuses publication into it unless it is an explicitly supported operation-owned checkout with custody. Never move a branch behind another index.
5. Durable intent/prepared pins and the TargetAttempt record (§10 rule 4) precede exact-old target CAS; a target CAS with an unknown outcome is never reissued. CAS loser returns stale and cannot reuse verification against a new target. When the main checkout holds the target, the winner runs non-destructive `read-tree -m -u <old destination> <candidate>` under main 50; non-overlapping dirty paths are tolerated and the checkout is left lagging per D-ADR0042 (G-099, preserved by owner decision Q7), recorded in the receipt as checkout-lagging rather than failing the land; ref success is never reported as checkout synced. No blind `reset --hard`.
6. Read back actual ref/tree/index, durably record receipt, release locks; consumer records actual `mergedSha`/`mergedInto` by operation id. Settlement failure is landed/consumer-settlement-pending, not permission to merge again. Land and cleanup remain separate. **Consumer settlement contract (M4 fold).** M4 held for an append failure known to precede its effect; its negative control showed that an append whose outcome is unknown (ack lost), retried without deduplication, produces two business settlements for one land. So the consumer's settlement is unique by `(repoIdentity, operationId, settlementKind)`; when an append outcome is unknown the consumer queries or replays that identity before any retry; a Git receipt or local success never mints a new settlement identity; cleanup runs only after durable consumer acknowledgement. Work/Event Store own this mechanism; Git states it as the precondition of its no-second-land guarantee.

Raw external Git ignores fgOS mutex. It is outside concurrency guarantees; pre/post drift is detected and preserved as recovery-required, never silently overwritten. A hook early probe is not full exclusion against raw checkout/reset/read-tree.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text:
1. Reserve target merge-slot 20; inspect true topology, source/target and target checkout status/index/MERGE_HEAD. Reject foreign state.
2. Create detached operation candidate under admin 40, release admin, construct merge from pinned target. Land conflict aborts candidate only; source and target preserved. Consumer transformations of non-event `.fgos`/decision documents produce declared candidate bytes, not Git-owned state meaning.
3. Consumer verifies/builds outside 50/60. Freeze tree/evidence before and after; any changed candidate/dependency setup invalidates evidence. No post-verify strip/renumber can publish bytes that do not match the bound digest. Pin candidate/bases against normal GC.
4. Reacquire required admin 40/main 50 in order; revalidate target/source, evidence and candidate; re-run the own-file-set clean gate (G-098/G-102: union of committed diff and declared footprint, normalized; whole-repo scope for land, subtree scope for return; `.fgos` never counts; fail-safe to every non-`.fgos` path when the set is absent; a staged rename blocks when either half is own) and return `main-checkout-dirty-mid-merge` without moving the ref when it fails. Never use main dirty bytes as merge input. Detect foreign linked checkout holding target; v1 refuses publication into it unless it is an explicitly supported operation-owned checkout with custody. Never move a branch behind another index.
5. Durable intent/prepared pins and the TargetAttempt record (§10 rule 4) precede exact-old target CAS; a target CAS with an unknown outcome is never reissued. CAS loser returns stale and cannot reuse verification against a new target. When the main checkout holds the target, the winner runs non-destructive `read-tree -m -u <old destination> <candidate>` under main 50; non-overlapping dirty paths are tolerated and the checkout is left lagging per D-ADR0042 (G-099, preserved by owner decision Q7), recorded in the receipt as checkout-lagging rather than failing the land; ref success is never reported as checkout synced. No blind `reset --hard`.
6. Read back actual ref/tree/index, durably record receipt, release locks; consumer records actual `mergedSha`/`mergedInto` by operation id. Settlement failure is landed/consumer-settlement-pending, not permission to merge again. Land and cleanup remain separate. **Consumer settlement contract (M4 fold).** M4 held for an append failure known to precede its effect; its negative control showed that an append whose outcome is unknown (ack lost), retried without deduplication, produces two business settlements for one land. So the consumer's settlement is unique by `(repoIdentity, operationId, settlementKind)`; when an append outcome is unknown the consumer queries or replays that identity before any retry; a Git receipt or local success never mints a new settlement identity; cleanup runs only after durable consumer acknowledgement. Work/Event Store own this mechanism; Git states it as the precondition of its no-second-land guarantee.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ### Driver state root
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
### Driver state root

2026-10-20 (phase 07 unit 18): `GitDriver::new` creates an absent state root through the same preparation as the `git-driver-directories` setup fix (mode 0700, empty `git-empty-hooks` mode 0500), so `fgos init`'s workspace read works before any other fgOS command has run. An existing root is only checked, never repaired here.

2026-10-19: the caller-owned trusted driver state root may contain `git-floor-verdict.json`, an optional floor-probe cache, alongside `git-empty-hooks` and temporary probe repositories. It is not WAL or operation evidence. Missing, unreadable, symlinked, inconsistent or differently keyed records cause probing again. The key binds the selected Git binary identity, host package version, probe implementation digest, floor contract, inherited `PATH`, `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and config-file identities. System/global paths come from the selected Git's `git var GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM/GLOBAL` discovery, shared with publication preflight; paths are never guessed from an installation prefix. Any include/includeIf directive disables persistent reuse (including missing or inactive targets), so conditional and included files cannot escape invalidation. The recorded probe names must match the required contract set exactly, without duplicates. A cache write failure only costs a later probe; no setup default, environment switch or doctor prerequisite is introduced.
