docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: `src/holder-lock/fences.mjs` is the body of the doctor check `lock-fences` and of its fix: `checkStopped({workspaces})` runs `quiesce-scan` per workspace (a root, or `{root, worktrees}` whose linked worktrees go in as `--dir`) and lists every blocker (an unreadable entry is a blocker; a platform that cannot scan answers `needs-attest`); `placeFences({fgosDir, workspaceRoot, worktrees, branches, providerRuntimeDir, stateRoot, owners})` places each fence by exclusive `mkdir` or by `link`, is idempotent, and stops with `v1-lock-present` and the path when a legacy lock file is in use (nobody's file is removed); `fenceStatus` reports which registry paths still lack their fence. Holder-lock sits below Git and never lists worktrees or branches itself: `worktrees` and `branches` are required, and the setup-layer caller (`src/setup/holder-lock-checks.mjs` `workspaceListing`) reads them through Git Inspect; both are empty outside a repository. The registry rows it fences are those of the `owners` (default: `4.2` and `4.4`); the machine-scope `install` path is resolved under the state root of §11 (`stateRoot`, else the process's own resolution) and fenced once per machine, so a second workspace finds it already fenced. The fix (`fenceCutover`) runs `checkStopped`, then `placeFences`, then `checkStopped` again to catch a process that started while the fences went in (it has met the fence and failed loudly, but it is still reported for a person to stop). A blocker on the first scan places nothing. The fix acts only in a workspace whose own activation (`.fgos/installation/activation.json`) runs a release that ships the lock registry in its legacy-node payload: fencing a workspace that still runs the legacy lock code would stop that workspace, so the order is activate first, then fence. The fix fences only the locks of the owners that payload registry names: a release whose registry has no `4.4` rows has an older `fgctl`, which still takes `.fgos/installation/activation.lock` and `<stateRoot>/install.lock`, so those two paths and `.fgos/observe/.lock` stay open until the release that ships the Rust callers is the activated one (a tombstone there would stop that older `fgctl` from upgrading the workspace). The provider ledgers are machine-wide: fencing them from one workspace makes every other workspace that still runs a release from before the cutover fail loudly at its next provider lock ("held by pid 1"), which is the A1 trade-off, so the cutover activates every workspace on the machine before any of them runs the fix. While the activation is older, the check's warning says the fix waits for it rather than pointing at `doctor --fix`. The scan treats any fgOS process on the machine as a blocker, so the fix only goes through once every session has stopped, which is the intent of the cutover.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 13. Setup, doctor and activation
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 13. Setup, doctor and activation
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 13. Setup, doctor and activation
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 13. Setup, doctor and activation

`fgos setup` creates `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks` with mode 0700 when they are missing and tightens an existing one to 0700 (fix `lock-dirs`), and registers one config default, `lock: {predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000}`: the merge adds the key only when it is missing and never overwrites a value the owner set (global first, then project on top). The key is a new top-level section; older releases do not validate unknown top-level keys, so writing it to `~/.fgos/config.json` does not break them. Setup runs every registered fix, so it also attempts the `lock-fences` cutover step, which places nothing under the conditions of §12.

`fgos doctor` checks, registered in `src/setup/registrations.mjs` with their bodies in `src/setup/holder-lock-checks.mjs`. Levels follow the doctor convention: `passed: false` fails, a message starting with `warning:` warns, `info:` is informational. Messages carry no timings, so two doctor runs over the same state print the same text:

| Check | Does | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `lock-kernel-semantics` | For `<fgosDir>/locks` and `<lockRoot>`: `--guarantee` through the route plus a two-process probe on that same mount (a child holds EX, the parent must see `held`; the child dies, the parent must see `free`) | Prints `{driver, exclusion, borrow, holders}`. `kernel` with a green probe passes (on Windows the probe runs over a `lock-hold` helper and the message shows `lockfileex`); a missing directory warns until setup creates it; a guarantee of `unsupported` (a platform with no driver) and a network filesystem (`none`) fail by name |
| `lock-borrow-vectors` | `fgos internal lock-borrow-vectors` | Any red vector or a red sibling check fails; `unavailable` (no git) fails too, as activation refuses it. Runs on every platform, with the Windows assertion of section 8.1 |
| `lock-holders` | The kernel's holder list for every existing lock file of this track's registry rows (run and account rows enumerated from their directories) | A holder warns with pid and cmdline unless it is a borrowed child of that lock (`FGOS_LOCK_FD=<name>:<slot>` in its environment), a process the host started (the `FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pin), or a fgOS payload by argv (`fgos`, `fgos-runner`, `fgos-gateway`, `bin/fgos.mjs`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`). A `<lock>.predecessor.json` whose domain is not judged dead, whose version is unknown, or which names a Windows job the host does not judge empty warns with the domain and the reason; a record written in another PID namespace judges `unknown` and keeps warning (and keeps the lock `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)`) until a person confirms the domain is gone and removes the record. Holders that cannot be listed are informational |
| `lock-fences` | `fenceStatus` | A registry path without its fence warns and names the fix (up to five paths, then a count); a legacy lock file still present is named. Covers the `activation`, `install` and `observe` paths next to the Node locks'. Fix: only under an activated holder-lock release (§12) and only for the owners its registry names, `checkStopped`, `placeFences`, `checkStopped`; with a blocker nothing is placed and the processes are listed |
| `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` | Reads `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` after the config merge | Prints the value and its source (`project`, `global` or `default`). Not an integer from 1 to 60000, or a config that does not parse, fails by name; absent passes with the default 2000 |
| `state-root` | `stateRoot`, `lockRoot` and the source, from Node and from the host for the same environment | A difference fails. A pinned root also prints what the host resolves without the pin |

The check `provider-capacity-lock-stale` is removed with its body: the provider-capacity ledger is no longer a mutex once the provider locks are kernel locks.

`fgctl` gates activation: right before it publishes the activation file on every path (init, upgrade, repair) it runs, through the crate it links itself and never under the candidate directory, the guarantee plus the two-process semantics probe for `<workspace>/.fgos/locks` and `<lockRoot>`, and the borrow vectors. On Linux and macOS a red probe or vector refuses the activation with `lock-kernel-semantics-failed` or `lock-borrow-vectors-failed` and the detail. The gate runs on Windows too, with the `fgctl` binary as its own helper; a platform whose driver reports itself unsupported refuses with `lock-kernel-semantics-failed` (`no holder-lock driver on <platform>`). A network filesystem is refused by name. There is no flag that turns the gate off. The manifest carries no `lockProtocol` field and there is no `lockProtocolFloor`.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 14. Main checkout: one door, one lock, borrowing through the description
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 14. Main checkout: one door, one lock, borrowing through the description
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 14. Main checkout: one door, one lock, borrowing through the description
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 14. Main checkout: one door, one lock, borrowing through the description

The main checkout is written by claim, merge, land and the `.fgos` checkpoint. Its single guard is the `main-checkout` mutex (rank 50, `<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock`, [registry](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json)): a kernel lock like every other mutex, so it has no TTL, no ambiguous state, no recognition of a holder by pid and no protocol marker. The kernel answers `held` or `free`; nothing in the component decides anything from a pid or a clock.

**One door.** Code reaches the main checkout through `withMainCheckout(scope, purpose, fn)`, which acquires the mutex in the caller's `LockScope` (section 9) and hands `fn` a `mainHandle`. A function that must write under the lock (the `.fgos` checkpoint) takes the handle as a required argument and never acquires by itself. A caller that already holds main (claim) passes its handle down; a merge holds only its slot while it merges and verifies in a temporary worktree, and calls `withMainCheckout` just for the checkpoint, the merge commit and the land. The order in a scope is fixed by rank: merge slot 20, `worktree-admin` 40, main checkout 50 (the state store locks sit at 60 in the registry).

**The merge slot** is a mutex per target ref (rank 20), at `<fgosDir>/locks/merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>.lock`; the encoded ref is what v1 already wrote. It serialises merges into one ref and is released after the merge, after main.

**Borrowing replaces `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`.** The holder runs every git child of a checkpoint or merge through `runBorrowed` (section 3), which gives the locked description to exactly that child in slot 3 with `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` and prepends `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json)). The `.githooks/pre-commit` hook, which git runs inside that child, is a borrower only when the three conditions of section 5 hold, checked by `fgos internal lock-fd --protocol 1 --borrowed-check <lock path>`. A borrower skips the activity beacon, because the lock proves who is committing. Anything else is a stranger: the hook probes `main-checkout` once with a description of its own, refuses when it is held, and never waits (git already holds `index.lock`, rank 55). The child cannot release the lock for the holder, cannot pass the description on beyond git's own hooks and cannot start anything in the background; the holder waits for the child before the transaction counts as done. The worker base env of a dispatch drops `FGOS_LOCK_FD`; a leaked variable gives nothing without the description.

`FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`, the holder record with its `ttlMs`, the recognition of the same identity as a refresh, the `protocol.json` marker and the `ambiguous` state of v1 do not exist in v3. A stuck holder is handled by section 17.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 15. Hot state mutex and porting events
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 15. Hot state mutex and porting events
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 15. Hot state mutex and porting events
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 15. Hot state mutex and porting events

The state store takes one transaction at a time per clone through `withStateTx(fgosDir, fn, {resource})` ([`src/state/hot-lock.mjs`](../../../src/state/hot-lock.mjs), contract [`hot-lock.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/hot-lock.v1.json)). `resource` is `state` (work events, claims, the state view) or `porting-events` (the porting log); both are registry rows of rank 60, kind `hot-mutex`. The mutex replaces `events.lock`, `runtime/claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`: claims and events are one critical section, so the worker-slot ceiling is checked in the same transaction as the claim. Code that must reach a hot resource gets the transaction object `tx` (`append`, `writeJson`, `writeText`, `rename`, `readJson`, `unlink`; paths confined to the `.fgos`), which is revoked when the callback returns.

**Fast path and record.** Acquire is `link()` of a whole temp file onto `<fgosDir>/locks/<resource>.hot`; release is `unlink`. The record is `{v, pid, startTime, bootId, pidNs, writer}`. A live holder is never taken over. Wait is 5 s, polling every 10 ms, then `hot-lock-timeout`.

**Cleanup of a dead holder** happens only under the kernel lock `<resource>.reclaim.lock` (the registry row's `v3Path`, taken through this facade): the judge of the whole tuple answers `dead` (a zombie counts as dead), the record is read again and its bytes equal what the judge saw, and only then is it unlinked. A record that does not parse, or whose judge answers `unknown` (no readable process table, a foreign pid namespace, a host that cannot be run), is never cleaned: the waiter times out with reason `lock-record-unreadable`, the `lock-record-unreadable` doctor check names the file, and a person who confirmed the holder is gone runs `fgos lock fence state` (section 17). On Windows the record has no `/proc` start time, so the holder's creation time (FILETIME, decimal, in `startTime`) comes from the host's process facts through `fgos internal process-observe`, asked once per process before any critical section; the judge reads the same route for a recorded pid, after a `kill(pid, 0)` that already says absent without a spawn, and reuses a live reading for 250 ms while a waiter polls (a reused reading can only keep a holder alive, never declare one dead). The verdicts are the table of the Rust judge: absent or exited is `dead`, the recorded creation time is `alive`, another creation time is a reused pid and `dead`, an unopenable process or a host that cannot be run is `unknown` and fails closed. The doctor check and `fgos lock fence` read the record through the same judge (`judgeHotRecord`).

**Critical section rules, thrown at once.** The callback is synchronous; a thenable result throws `state-tx-async`. Starting a child process inside the section (any `child_process` export, including named ESM imports) throws `exec-under-hot-lock` at the call; acquiring a hot mutex again in the same process throws `hot-lock-reentry` without waiting. Values that need git or the host (`mainFgosDir`, `head`, the writer identity) are read before the lock and passed in as `prefetched`. There is no switch that turns the guard off.

**Lock order.** Hot mutexes sit at rank 60, above the main checkout (50): a claim reads HEAD, takes the `state` transaction for the check and the claim record, and takes main only around the `.fgos` checkpoint, never inside the state transaction.

Nothing in the repo-lock core (sections 14, 16) imports the event log, a shard or `withStateTx`; the `.fgos` checkpoint of the main door stays a detachable adapter. The event file format, `merge=union`, `.gitattributes` and the `.fgos` strip rule are untouched: they belong to the event store cutover ([event store spec](../event-store/spec.md) section 13 names `withStateTx` as the Work gate).

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 16. `worktree-admin`
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 16. `worktree-admin`
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 16. `worktree-admin`

`worktree-admin` is a mutex (rank 40, `<fgosDir>/locks/worktree-admin.lock`) with no v1 predecessor and no fence. It wraps every fgOS call of `git worktree add`, `git worktree remove`, `git worktree move` (relocate) and `git worktree prune`. For remove and relocate, the dirty-check of the worktree, the destroy or move, and the registration change run under one hold of the lock, so no other worktree administration can run between the check and the effect (Git lessons G-042, G-155). It stays one lock: there is no second admin lock, and read-only listing takes none. Rank 40 is below main checkout (50), so no wrapped worktree command runs while main is held: a claim creates its worktree after it has released main; a merge creates its temporary worktree under the merge slot (20), before it takes main.

Amended 2026-10-17 by owner decision (Git G0 Q6); implemented by the Rust Git Worktree port in phase 03 (2026-10-19), including operation-specific prune/repair under the same rank-40 scope. The public create verb uses this door; runner, session and integration callers move onto the Worktree port in Git phase 07. Status: implemented in the port; complete once the one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, Git spec §12) reports zero undeclared worktree writers (on 2026-10-20 one raw `git worktree remove --force` remained in `bin/fgos.mjs`, owned by the last phase 07 unit). Before this amendment the lock wrapped `git worktree add` only, and `remove` and `prune` stayed unwrapped because they had no recorded incident. The Git component spec ([docs/platform/git/spec.md](../git/spec.md) §5) states which Git operations take this lock and which locks a caller may already hold.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 17. `fgos lock fence`
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 17. `fgos lock fence`
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 17. `fgos lock fence`
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 17. `fgos lock fence`

A hung live holder is never taken over. `fgos lock fence <name>` is the one door a person uses for it, and it replaces `unlock --force`:

1. It lists every process that holds a description of the lock file (Linux: `holders()`) and shows each with pid and cmdline.
2. It asks the person to confirm.
3. It sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to each by identity ([process spec](../process/spec.md)); the lock releases when they are dead. There is no path that takes a lock from a live holder.
4. Where holders are `unlistable` (macOS, Windows) the person stops the process and runs `fgos lock fence <name> --attest-stopped`, which only re-checks by try-lock.
5. A hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`, section 15) is held by its record file, not by a kernel lock the holder keeps. `fgos lock fence state` reads the record: a holder it proves alive is ended like any other holder (after confirmation); a record that does not parse, or whose holder cannot be judged here (a process the Windows host cannot open, a foreign pid namespace), is removed only with `--attest-stopped`. The record is removed under the reclaim lock and only while it still holds the bytes that were read, so a holder that arrived meanwhile is never cleared.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 18. Cutover of the main checkout and the merge slot
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 18. Cutover of the main checkout and the merge slot

The same stop-everything rule as section 12 applies; each lock moves to its new path and the legacy path is deleted in the same phase. Fences, all tombstones placed once by exclusive `mkdir` through `placeFences`:

| Lock | Legacy path made a tombstone directory |
|---|---|
| `main-checkout` | `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` |
| `merge-slot` | `.fgos/merge-slot--<ref>.lock` for every `refs/heads/*` that exists at cutover |
| `state` | `.fgos/events.lock` and `.fgos/runtime/claims.lock` |
| `porting-events` | `.fgos/porting/events.lock` |

`worktree-admin` has none. An older release that meets a tombstone fails with a raw `EISDIR` (measured with the real code of the cutover's base commit: `withEventsLock`, `withClaimsLock`, `acquireMainCheckoutLock`, the old hook and the old merge slot all throw it); that is accepted for a single user and noted in the changelog.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 19. Known limits
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 19. Known limits
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 19. Known limits
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 19. Known limits

- Git Worktree remove/move cannot acquire rank 30 while holding rank 40. It rechecks custody and live cwd immediately before TargetAttempt and again before the Git call, but a new rank-30 acquirer can still race the final probe. Cross-user unreadable cwd and privileged actors are outside its same-user process guarantee; shared cross-user checkout custody is not certified.

- A live holder that is wedged keeps its lock until it exits: a dispatcher stuck on a cwd blocks that cwd with no time limit (the legacy lock had a 4-hour ttl and a reconcile clear; `dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` now only reports held or free). The worker it started is still killed at its run timeout.
- A hung live holder is never taken over. A person fences it (section 17); the lock releases when it dies.
- `holders()` is `unlistable` on macOS and Windows, so `lock-holders` and the leftover kill of `run_borrowed` rely on the process group there (best-effort).
- The supervisor declares its attempt domain on the cwd lease on every platform. A best-effort `linux-pgroup` or `macos-tree` record cannot prove successor custody after controller death; Execution refuses that worktree even when the group appears empty. A crash while a borrow runs on Windows costs the next acquire about 120-170 ms.
- The dispatch cwd lock keeps the `fgosDir` scope: two workspaces whose `.fgos` directories differ do not exclude each other on one cwd.
- A borrower hook's `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` on an inherited description also succeeds when nobody holds the lock; that only happens when the API hands over a description it has not locked, which is a programming error, since the API only passes a description after acquire.
- Execution retains one dispatch-cwd lease across a Unit run, provider failover, runner commit, receipt and handoff. Commit git/hook children and the Unit verify command borrow it. Unknown launch/recovery failures release the controller copy without clearing its predecessor. Workflow preserves the refused checkout and branch and redispatches once into a fresh worktree from the recorded base; explicit `fgos run --worktree` stops with the typed cause.
- `FGOS_HOST_BIN` is inherited, so a child uses its parent's host binary; a release whose route speaks another protocol answers `host-version-mismatch` and the facade fails closed.
- A copy-holder that changes the lock type on the shared description (`LOCK_SH` on an exclusive copy) re-stamps the record with its own pid and briefly drops the lock; it is then indistinguishable from a later acquirer, is not killed, and shows in `lock-holders` as a non-fgOS holder until it exits.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: Stranded custody record: manual recovery until Git phase 03
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: Stranded custody record: manual recovery until Git phase 03
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ### Stranded custody record: manual recovery until Git phase 03
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
### Stranded custody record: manual recovery until Git phase 03

The dispatch-cwd key includes the real cwd's device, inode and nanosecond birth time, so deleting a worktree does not transfer an inode-only predecessor record to a new directory. Existing symlink spellings still share one key. This changes the key: use the phase's stop-everything cutover; old and new controllers must never coexist.

Until Git phase 03 owns removal/recovery, preserve the refused checkout and use a fresh worktree. To recover that same checkout manually: stop all dispatchers for it, identify the exact lock path in the refusal, inspect its `.predecessor.json` with `fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state <lock-path>`, fence the recorded producer and every possible descendant (including escaped sessions), and verify no writer remains. Only under that quiescence may an operator archive/remove that **predecessor record**; retain the lock file itself. An empty group or a free kernel lock alone does not authorize this action. Unprovable process membership means keep the record and use the replacement tree. Do not automate record deletion by age or PID liveness.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 20. Lịch sử quyết định
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 20. Lịch sử quyết định
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 20. Lịch sử quyết định

- **2026-10-19 — Release settle supersedes same-day full scans on admission and borrow return, and qualifies §1's no-pid wording.** Coordinator initially selected table-first, recipient-until-release, and no `#[must_use]`. Kernel verification disproved the negative one-read proof: 256 real flocks, a 1 MiB request, first read 4,045 bytes/76 records and a second read 4,050 bytes. Coordinator then selected table-first positive detection plus the inode-checked shared-probe fallback, accepting its brief Try-contention window (§5). Exclusive Linux `release` and `Drop` share that settle; borrows/admission retain one lagged `Since` pass and refuse missing creation marks rather than using a full scan. Full descriptor scans remain only for uncertain release/leaks and Node's unknown-history drain. Unreadable facts never imply clearance. The component reuses process identities, fdinfo parsing and a shared kill/wait loop; no persistent pid ownership or kept duplicate. See [counsel](../../../plans/reports/counsel-261019-0204-holder-lock-release-settle.md) and [implementation evidence](../../../plans/reports/phase-lead-261019-0204-git-perf-release-settle.md).

- **2026-10-15 — Thiết kế nền bản 3 (r1): kernel lock trên open file description thay mọi lock TTL/pid.** Lock thuộc description, không thuộc pid: không tái dùng pid, không boot id, không TTL, không record cần dọn, không GC; con kế thừa description lúc spawn nên mượn quyền không có khe; kernel trả lời "có ai giữ không" bằng try-lock. Bằng chứng: probe kernel lock trên Linux thật (giữ sau khi helper thoát, hai description cùng process loại trừ, SIGKILL nhả ngay, mượn qua git thật với owner bị SIGKILL). Thiết kế và probe: [design r6](../../../plans/reports/design-261016-1238-lock-and-run-supervisor-foundation-v3-r6.md) §6, §12.1.
- **2026-10-16 — r2, r3: ba vòng phản biện (kongming, Astra, Argon).** Nhận: luật description (Rust kế thừa fd ≥ 3 không `CLOEXEC`; `git gc --auto` giữ lock sau commit; fd mượn rò qua shell nền) → `FD_CLOEXEC`, `O_RDWR`, close-only, API mượn tắt gc, test rò trên route thật, doctor `lock-holders`; tombstone không phải hàng rào chung → kiểm kê theo hình dạng giao thức, thế hệ chặn cho ledger, tombstone cả `path.resolve` lẫn `realpath`; zombie bị coi là sống và record thiếu pid bị coi là chết → sửa ở process facts; `probe` dùng `LOCK_SH` để quét adopt không cản holder (kongming N6); vân tay runtime tắt mượn khi đổi git/host bị bác vì tự chặn commit của fgOS → check `lock-borrow-vectors`, đỏ = FAIL, không có chế độ tắt mượn (kongming M4). Design §14.
- **2026-10-16 — r4: yêu cầu chạy trên Linux, macOS, Windows.** Cổng lock trung lập OS, mỗi nền một driver, mức bảo đảm khai báo và doctor báo mức; không còn "fail trên Windows"; spike X1 (Windows) và X2 (macOS) đo trên máy thật trước khi viết driver. r4 còn giữ R-dual + quiescence hai pha + sàn `lockProtocolFloor` và lịch trace → cảnh báo → ném cho thứ tự lock (§6.5, §6.8).
- **2026-10-16 — r5: luật miền của holder trước (6.0.1).** Đo trên Windows thật: lock trống 0,2 ms sau khi holder bị giết nhưng process cuối trong job chết sau 3,9 ms → một vi phạm. `acquire` chỉ trả handle khi kernel lock đã giữ VÀ miền process của holder trước đã rỗng; record `predecessor.json`; r5 chờ cạn tới `lock.predecessorDrainMs`. Design §12.10.
- **2026-10-16 — r6: kết thúc ngay, bỏ chờ cạn.** Lần đo hai: với job do supervisor giữ, 0/50 vi phạm nhưng contender luôn chờ đủ 2000 ms (p50 2006,8 ms). Chọn phương án B: holder chỉ nhả khi miền của mình rỗng (bước 0), người sau thấy miền trước chưa rỗng thì kết thúc ngay; `lock.predecessorDrainMs` bỏ, thay bằng `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` chỉ giới hạn chờ signaled. Windows cần người giữ job thứ hai; đường dự phòng Toolhelp đo 0/50 vi phạm, chờ thêm p95 8,7 ms. Design §6.0.1, §12.11, §12.12.
- **2026-10-16 — Quyết định của anh (plan 4.2, thay một phần thiết kế).** A1: cutover dừng-toàn-bộ thay R-dual và quiescence hai pha; một user, state xoá làm lại được; chuyển mỗi lock và xoá đường v1 trong cùng phase; không marker họ, không sàn, không phase xoá v1 riêng. A2: Windows chưa có driver thì các lock này báo `unsupported`, không lùi về v1; driver Windows chỉ viết sau khi các probe 6.0.1 xanh trên máy thật; macOS bật driver `flock` ngay (X2 đã đo), vẫn chặn ở activate bằng vector mượn và probe ngữ nghĩa. A3: sai thứ tự lock ném lỗi ngay, không lịch trace → cảnh báo → ném; full `npm test` và dogfood lộ vi phạm, sửa trong phase gây ra. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1104-holder-lock-kernel-lock-foundation/plan.md).
- **2026-10-16 — Lead tự quyết (plan 4.2).** D1: spec ở `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` và `docs/platform/process/spec.md`, theo tiền lệ Session Identity. D2: registry lock là file dữ liệu `lock-registry.v1.json`, chốt ở phase đầu, Rust và Node cùng đọc. D3: primitive cho gate (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) để run supervisor làm, 4.2 không có consumer. D4: `fgctl` chạy vector mượn và probe ngữ nghĩa bằng crate nó tự link, trước publish. D5: route nội bộ kiểm `--protocol 1`, lệch → `host-version-mismatch`. D6: account lock giữ bất biến "con probe còn sống thì không giành" bằng `runBorrowed`. D7: bỏ `lockProtocolFloor` và trường `lockProtocol` của manifest (hàng rào đã làm binary cũ fail to tiếng). D8: luật 6.0.1 cài một lần trong lõi cổng và route; ở 4.2 chỉ miền `linux-gate` có cài đặt; luật nhả trên Linux: `run_borrowed` không khai miền, phần còn sót là process khác còn giữ description; macOS: process group của con.
- **2026-10-17 — Cutover từng lock, sửa registry theo code thật.** Registry: `advance` và `recovery` chuyển vào `<run>/locks/` (đường cũ chính là chỗ đặt tombstone, giữ nguyên thì mọi run đã rào đều `EISDIR`); `dispatch-cwd` khoá theo `dev:ino` sau `realpath` thay `encodeURIComponent(cwd)` (worktree qua symlink là một lock); gói npm và payload legacy-node mang file registry. Lock tài khoản provider và `provider-state` thành mutex phạm vi máy; con probe/renewal chạy qua `runBorrowed` nên holder chết mà con còn sống thì lock vẫn giữ. `reconcile.lock` thành kernel mutex; `clear-cwd-lock` chỉ còn báo held/free. Check `provider-capacity-lock-stale` và `inspectProviderCapacityLock` xoá cùng lúc.
- **2026-10-17 — Doctor và setup của holder-lock.** Fix `lock-fences` chỉ chạy khi activation của chính workspace đã là release có registry (activate trước, rào sau): `fgos setup` chạy mọi fix, và một fix không điều kiện sẽ rào ledger provider thật dưới `$HOME` từ bất kỳ test hay lần setup nào trên máy đang yên, làm hỏng các workspace còn chạy code cũ. Probe hai process của doctor viết lại trong Node bằng chính route `lock-fd` (thân Rust ở `semantics.rs` không có route); message không mang thời gian để hai lần doctor trên cùng trạng thái in giống nhau. `lock-holders` nhận diện process fgOS bằng pin `FGOS_STATE_ROOT`, argv payload, và `FGOS_LOCK_FD=<lock>:` cho con mượn. Thư mục lock do fix `lock-dirs` tạo (setup chỉ tạo qua fix), cả hai ở mode 0700.

- **2026-10-16 — Quyết định của anh (plan main-door, thay M5 của thiết kế).** Sai thứ tự lock ném lỗi ngay; bỏ lịch trace → cảnh báo → ném (design §6.5). Full `npm test` và dogfood lộ call site sai, sửa trong phase gây ra; không có biến môi trường bật tắt gác. Spec: mục 9. Phần gác `hot-lock-reentry` / `exec-under-hot-lock` thuộc mutex nóng (mục 15). [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-16 — Lead tự quyết (plan main-door, phần khoá repo).** D1: cửa main checkout ở module mới `src/runner/repo-locks.mjs` (`withMainCheckout` trao `mainHandle`, `withMergeTargetSlot`, `withWorktreeAdmin`); phần main của `main-checkout-lock.mjs` bị xoá, checkpoint `.fgos` là adapter tháo rời nhận handle. D4: hàng rào merge slot là tombstone cho mọi `refs/heads/*` có lúc cutover; registry giữ chỗ giữ `<ref>`, caller truyền ref đã `encodeURIComponent` như v1. D5: `withLockRetry` giữ tên và cờ `--wait`/`--no-wait`, thân chờ bằng facade, bỏ ETA/TTL. D6: hook pre-commit nhận borrower qua `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` + `--borrowed-check`, không thì `probe` main một lần, `held` thì từ chối; beacon W1' giữ nguyên. D7: `fgos lock fence <name>` thay verb `unlock` (xoá), skill `fgos-unlock` đổi tên `fgos-lock-fence`, `lock-status` đọc registry. D8: `worktree-admin` chỉ bọc `git worktree add` (Amended 2026-10-17 by owner decision (Git G0 Q6); implementation lands with the Git component: nay bọc add, remove, move và prune, xem mục 16). Spec: mục 14, 16–18. Nguồn: [plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md), `packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json`.
- **2026-10-17 — Rào chắn F10: phần state của 4.3 chờ hội đồng event store.** Mutex nóng `state`/`porting-events`, `stateTx`, gộp `events.lock` + `claims.lock` và trần claim không được chốt ở đây; luật L3 đã chạm ngưỡng xem lại. Phần khoá repo không import event log, shard, `events.lock` hay `stateTx`; mọi test của nó pass với adapter checkpoint rỗng; `merge=union`, `.gitattributes` và luật strip `.fgos` không đổi. Đã được thay bằng mục kế tiếp sau khi hội đồng event store xong.
- **2026-10-17 — Phần state của 4.3 (wave S), sau quyết định event store D-ADR0055.** `withStateTx` trên mutex nóng `state` chính là cổng Work của event store, nên giữ nguyên thiết kế: `state` gộp `events.lock` + `runtime/claims.lock`, `porting-events` thay `porting/events.lock`; bản ghi nóng là tuple đầy đủ, dọn holder chết chỉ dưới kernel lock `<resource>.reclaim.lock`, bản ghi không đọc được hoặc `judge` ra `unknown` không bao giờ bị dọn (thoát bằng `fgos lock fence`); subprocess trong vùng găng và lấy lại mutex ném ngay; trần worker kiểm trong `state` ngay trước claim, main chỉ giữ quanh checkpoint (một commit). Windows fail closed tới khi có judge Windows (plan 4.4b). Ba đường cũ (`events.lock`, `runtime/claims.lock`, `porting/events.lock`) thành tombstone; check doctor `lock-record-unreadable`. Không đổi định dạng event, `merge=union`, `.gitattributes`, luật strip `.fgos`; không thêm hàng registry của event store. Spec: mục 15, 18. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-16 — Lead tự quyết (plan 4.4a: fgctl và Observe gọi từ Rust).** `activation`, `install`, `observe` thành kernel lock: `activation.lock` ở `<fgosDir>/locks/` (mutex, rank 80, repo), `install.lock` ở `<stateRoot>/locks/` (machine), `observe.lock` ở `<fgosDir>/locks/` chờ 5 giây, không TTL, snapshot shard ghi dưới lock. Holder bị giết thì lock nhả ngay. Ba đường cũ (`.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock`, `.fgos/observe/.lock`) thành thư mục tombstone, fgctl/fgos cũ dừng có lỗi. Tới khi main checkout được cutover, fgctl kiểm main checkout bằng `probe` (shared, không chặn, không giữ) cộng đọc v1, và coi thư mục tombstone ở `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` là "đã chuyển". Windows: `fgctl init`/`upgrade`/`repair` từ chối với `lock-driver-unavailable` cho tới khi có driver Windows, không lùi về file cũ. D1: ba lock là ba hàng registry riêng (`activation`, `install`, `observe`), cả ba mutex hạng 80, hàng rào tombstone. D2: `check_main_checkout_lock` của `fgctl` = `probe(main-checkout)` không giữ, cộng đường đọc v1 chỉ thêm nhánh tombstone; không giữ main mutex qua publish vì `run_tail` chạy `fgos setup` có thể checkpoint main. D3: Rust không giữ `LockScope`; thứ tự cố định trong code: `probe(main-checkout)` → `activation`; `install` chỉ giữ trong `stage_release`, nhả trước `activation`, hai lock hạng 80 không lồng nhau. D4: ghi shard snapshot của Observe đi dưới observe lock (hai process cùng writer id có thể xen dòng). D5: Windows trước driver Windows: `lock-driver-unavailable`, không lùi về v1. D6: giữ tên kiểu công khai `ActivationLockGuard`, `InstallLockGuard`, `StoreLockGuard` và biến thể lỗi `ActivationLockHeld`, `AlreadyInProgress`, `observe-lock-timeout`; guard bọc handle, `Drop` chỉ đóng description. Hàng rào: `placeFences`/`fenceStatus` phủ cả owner `4.4` (tombstone ghi `by: fgos 4.4`), đường `install` giải dưới state root và đặt một lần cho máy; fix `lock-fences` chỉ rào các owner mà registry trong payload của release đang activate nêu tên, vì `fgctl` cũ vẫn lấy `activation.lock` và `install.lock` ở đường cũ và một tombstone ở đó chặn nó nâng cấp workspace. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-fgctl-rust-callers-on-holder-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-17 — Driver Windows (plan 4.4b).** `LockFileEx` trong process giữ lock; Node giữ lock qua một helper `lock-hold` cho mỗi lock; mượn lock chạy con trong job có tên, không đưa handle. Guarantee Windows là `lockfileex`/`kernel`, `job-scoped` là mức mượn (lệch với ghi chú bàn giao 4.4a, nói doctor báo `job-scoped`). Miền `windows-job` có hai view (job, contender), quy tắc hợp ba nguồn đọc lại mỗi lần poll, fail closed với pid sống mà không mở được, người giữ job thứ hai (`job-keeper`), và route chỉ-đọc `--predecessor-state` cho doctor. Cổng `fgctl` và doctor chạy trên Windows; nền không có driver thì fail theo tên. Vector mượn trên Windows khẳng định bằng handle `SYNCHRONIZE` riêng. macOS không đổi; fence trên Windows dùng đường attested. Bằng chứng: [probe](../../../plans/reports/probe-261017-0710-windows-predecessor-all-owners-dead-race.md), [red-team](../../../plans/reports/red-team-261017-1330-windows-lockfileex-driver-plan-review.md). [Plan](../../../plans/261017-1256-windows-lockfileex-driver-and-macos-handoff/plan.md).
- **2026-10-17 — Quyết định của anh (Git G0 Q6): `worktree-admin` bọc add, remove, move, prune.** Bài học G-042 và G-155 của component Git đòi kiểm bẩn tới lúc huỷ nằm dưới một quyền sở hữu; D8 chỉ bọc `git worktree add` nên remove/relocate/prune là khe hở có tên. Mở rộng tập bọc của chính lock hạng 40, không thêm lock admin thứ hai, không đổi rank, đường dẫn hay hàng registry. Cài đặt đi cùng component Git. Spec: mục 16; [Git spec](../git/spec.md) §5, §18.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: - **2026-10-19 — Release settle supersedes same-day full scans on admission and borrow return, and qualifies §1's no-pid wording.** Coordinator initially selected table-first, recipient-until-release, and no `#[must_use]`. Kernel verification disproved the negative one-read proof: 256 real flocks, a 1 MiB request, first read 4,045 bytes/76 records and a second read 4,050 bytes. Coordinator then selected table-first positive detection plus the inode-checked shared-probe fallback, accepting its brief Try-contention window (§5). Exclusive Linux `release` and `Drop` share that settle; borrows/admission retain one lagged `Since` pass and refuse missing creation marks rather than using a full scan. Full descriptor scans remain only for uncertain release/leaks and Node's unknown-history drain. Unreadable facts never imply clearance. The component reuses process identities, fdinfo parsing and a shared kill/wait loop; no persistent pid ownership or kept duplicate. See [counsel](../../../plans/reports/counsel-261019-0204-holder-lock-release-settle.md) and [implementation evidence](../../../plans/reports/phase-lead-261019-0204-git-perf-release-settle.md).

D2: registry lock là file dữ liệu `lock-registry.v1.json`, chốt ở phase đầu, Rust và Node cùng đọc. D3: primitive cho gate (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) để run supervisor làm, 4.2 không có consumer. D4: `fgctl` chạy vector mượn và probe ngữ nghĩa bằng crate nó tự link, trước publish. D5: route nội bộ kiểm `--protocol 1`, lệch → `host-version-mismatch`. D6: account lock giữ bất biến "con probe còn sống thì không giành" bằng `runBorrowed`. D7: bỏ `lockProtocolFloor` và trường `lockProtocol` của manifest (hàng rào đã làm binary cũ fail to tiếng). D8: luật 6.0.1 cài một lần trong lõi cổng và route; ở 4.2 chỉ miền `linux-gate` có cài đặt; luật nhả trên Linux: `run_borrowed` không khai miền, phần còn sót là process khác còn giữ description; macOS: process group của con.
- **2026-10-17 — Cutover từng lock, sửa registry theo code thật.** Registry: `advance` và `recovery` chuyển vào `<run>/locks/` (đường cũ chính là chỗ đặt tombstone, giữ nguyên thì mọi run đã rào đều `EISDIR`); `dispatch-cwd` khoá theo `dev:ino` sau `realpath` thay `encodeURIComponent(cwd)` (worktree qua symlink là một lock); gói npm và payload legacy-node mang file registry. Lock tài khoản provider và `provider-state` thành mutex phạm vi máy; con probe/renewal chạy qua `runBorrowed` nên holder chết mà con còn sống thì lock vẫn giữ. `reconcile.lock` thành kernel mutex; `clear-cwd-lock` chỉ còn báo held/free. Check `provider-capacity-lock-stale` và `inspectProviderCapacityLock` xoá cùng lúc.
- **2026-10-17 — Doctor và setup của holder-lock.** Fix `lock-fences` chỉ chạy khi activation của chính workspace đã là release có registry (activate trước, rào sau): `fgos setup` chạy mọi fix, và một fix không điều kiện sẽ rào ledger provider thật dưới `$HOME` từ bất kỳ test hay lần setup nào trên máy đang yên, làm hỏng các workspace còn chạy code cũ. Probe hai process của doctor viết lại trong Node bằng chính route `lock-fd` (thân Rust ở `semantics.rs` không có route); message không mang thời gian để hai lần doctor trên cùng trạng thái in giống nhau. `lock-holders` nhận diện process fgOS bằng pin `FGOS_STATE_ROOT`, argv payload, và `FGOS_LOCK_FD=<lock>:` cho con mượn. Thư mục lock do fix `lock-dirs` tạo (setup chỉ tạo qua fix), cả hai ở mode 0700.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text:
- **2026-10-16 — Quyết định của anh (plan main-door, thay M5 của thiết kế).** Sai thứ tự lock ném lỗi ngay; bỏ lịch trace → cảnh báo → ném (design §6.5). Full `npm test` và dogfood lộ call site sai, sửa trong phase gây ra; không có biến môi trường bật tắt gác. Spec: mục 9. Phần gác `hot-lock-reentry` / `exec-under-hot-lock` thuộc mutex nóng (mục 15). [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-16 — Lead tự quyết (plan main-door, phần khoá repo).** D1: cửa main checkout ở module mới `src/runner/repo-locks.mjs` (`withMainCheckout` trao `mainHandle`, `withMergeTargetSlot`, `withWorktreeAdmin`); phần main của `main-checkout-lock.mjs` bị xoá, checkpoint `.fgos` là adapter tháo rời nhận handle. D4: hàng rào merge slot là tombstone cho mọi `refs/heads/*` có lúc cutover; registry giữ chỗ giữ `<ref>`, caller truyền ref đã `encodeURIComponent` như v1. D5: `withLockRetry` giữ tên và cờ `--wait`/`--no-wait`, thân chờ bằng facade, bỏ ETA/TTL. D6: hook pre-commit nhận borrower qua `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` + `--borrowed-check`, không thì `probe` main một lần, `held` thì từ chối; beacon W1' giữ nguyên. D7: `fgos lock fence <name>` thay verb `unlock` (xoá), skill `fgos-unlock` đổi tên `fgos-lock-fence`, `lock-status` đọc registry. D8: `worktree-admin` chỉ bọc `git worktree add` (Amended 2026-10-17 by owner decision (Git G0 Q6); implementation lands with the Git component: nay bọc add, remove, move và prune, xem mục 16). Spec: mục 14, 16–18. Nguồn: [plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md), `packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json`.
- **2026-10-17 — Rào chắn F10: phần state của 4.3 chờ hội đồng event store.** Mutex nóng `state`/`porting-events`, `stateTx`, gộp `events.lock` + `claims.lock` và trần claim không được chốt ở đây; luật L3 đã chạm ngưỡng xem lại. Phần khoá repo không import event log, shard, `events.lock` hay `stateTx`; mọi test của nó pass với adapter checkpoint rỗng; `merge=union`, `.gitattributes` và luật strip `.fgos` không đổi. Đã được thay bằng mục kế tiếp sau khi hội đồng event store xong.
- **2026-10-17 — Phần state của 4.3 (wave S), sau quyết định event store D-ADR0055.** `withStateTx` trên mutex nóng `state` chính là cổng Work của event store, nên giữ nguyên thiết kế: `state` gộp `events.lock` + `runtime/claims.lock`, `porting-events` thay `porting/events.lock`; bản ghi nóng là tuple đầy đủ, dọn holder chết chỉ dưới kernel lock `<resource>.reclaim.lock`, bản ghi không đọc được hoặc `judge` ra `unknown` không bao giờ bị dọn (thoát bằng `fgos lock fence`); subprocess trong vùng găng và lấy lại mutex ném ngay; trần worker kiểm trong `state` ngay trước claim, main chỉ giữ quanh checkpoint (một commit). Windows fail closed tới khi có judge Windows (plan 4.4b). Ba đường cũ (`events.lock`, `runtime/claims.lock`, `porting/events.lock`) thành tombstone; check doctor `lock-record-unreadable`. Không đổi định dạng event, `merge=union`, `.gitattributes`, luật strip `.fgos`; không thêm hàng registry của event store. Spec: mục 15, 18. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-main-checkout-single-door-hot-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-16 — Lead tự quyết (plan 4.4a: fgctl và Observe gọi từ Rust).** `activation`, `install`, `observe` thành kernel lock: `activation.lock` ở `<fgosDir>/locks/` (mutex, rank 80, repo), `install.lock` ở `<stateRoot>/locks/` (machine), `observe.lock` ở `<fgosDir>/locks/` chờ 5 giây, không TTL, snapshot shard ghi dưới lock. Holder bị giết thì lock nhả ngay. Ba đường cũ (`.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock`, `.fgos/observe/.lock`) thành thư mục tombstone, fgctl/fgos cũ dừng có lỗi. Tới khi main checkout được cutover, fgctl kiểm main checkout bằng `probe` (shared, không chặn, không giữ) cộng đọc v1, và coi thư mục tombstone ở `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` là "đã chuyển". Windows: `fgctl init`/`upgrade`/`repair` từ chối với `lock-driver-unavailable` cho tới khi có driver Windows, không lùi về file cũ. D1: ba lock là ba hàng registry riêng (`activation`, `install`, `observe`), cả ba mutex hạng 80, hàng rào tombstone. D2: `check_main_checkout_lock` của `fgctl` = `probe(main-checkout)` không giữ, cộng đường đọc v1 chỉ thêm nhánh tombstone; không giữ main mutex qua publish vì `run_tail` chạy `fgos setup` có thể checkpoint main. D3: Rust không giữ `LockScope`; thứ tự cố định trong code: `probe(main-checkout)` → `activation`; `install` chỉ giữ trong `stage_release`, nhả trước `activation`, hai lock hạng 80 không lồng nhau. D4: ghi shard snapshot của Observe đi dưới observe lock (hai process cùng writer id có thể xen dòng). D5: Windows trước driver Windows: `lock-driver-unavailable`, không lùi về v1. D6: giữ tên kiểu công khai `ActivationLockGuard`, `InstallLockGuard`, `StoreLockGuard` và biến thể lỗi `ActivationLockHeld`, `AlreadyInProgress`, `observe-lock-timeout`; guard bọc handle, `Drop` chỉ đóng description. Hàng rào: `placeFences`/`fenceStatus` phủ cả owner `4.4` (tombstone ghi `by: fgos 4.4`), đường `install` giải dưới state root và đặt một lần cho máy; fix `lock-fences` chỉ rào các owner mà registry trong payload của release đang activate nêu tên, vì `fgctl` cũ vẫn lấy `activation.lock` và `install.lock` ở đường cũ và một tombstone ở đó chặn nó nâng cấp workspace. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1306-fgctl-rust-callers-on-holder-lock/plan.md).
- **2026-10-17 — Driver Windows (plan 4.4b).** `LockFileEx` trong process giữ lock; Node giữ lock qua một helper `lock-hold` cho mỗi lock; mượn lock chạy con trong job có tên, không đưa handle. Guarantee Windows là `lockfileex`/`kernel`, `job-scoped` là mức mượn (lệch với ghi chú bàn giao 4.4a, nói doctor báo `job-scoped`). Miền `windows-job` có hai view (job, contender), quy tắc hợp ba nguồn đọc lại mỗi lần poll, fail closed với pid sống mà không mở được, người giữ job thứ hai (`job-keeper`), và route chỉ-đọc `--predecessor-state` cho doctor. Cổng `fgctl` và doctor chạy trên Windows; nền không có driver thì fail theo tên. Vector mượn trên Windows khẳng định bằng handle `SYNCHRONIZE` riêng. macOS không đổi; fence trên Windows dùng đường attested. Bằng chứng: [probe](../../../plans/reports/probe-261017-0710-windows-predecessor-all-owners-dead-race.md), [red-team](../../../plans/reports/red-team-261017-1330-windows-lockfileex-driver-plan-review.md). [Plan](../../../plans/261017-1256-windows-lockfileex-driver-and-macos-handoff/plan.md).
- **2026-10-17 — Quyết định của anh (Git G0 Q6): `worktree-admin` bọc add, remove, move, prune.** Bài học G-042 và G-155 của component Git đòi kiểm bẩn tới lúc huỷ nằm dưới một quyền sở hữu; D8 chỉ bọc `git worktree add` nên remove/relocate/prune là khe hở có tên. Mở rộng tập bọc của chính lock hạng 40, không thêm lock admin thứ hai, không đổi rank, đường dẫn hay hàng registry. Cài đặt đi cùng component Git. Spec: mục 16; [Git spec](../git/spec.md) §5, §18.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.text: ## 1. Purpose
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
## 1. Purpose

The doctor/fix registry is the extension point for environment readiness. Modules register checks, fixes, and config defaults instead of adding one-off repair logic.

Target architecture has no separate `fgos setup` verb for workspace onboarding. `fgctl init` is the one-command workspace onboarding orchestrator; after activation it invokes active local `fgos init`, `fgos doctor --fix`, and `fgos doctor`. Legacy shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior under the explicit deprecated fallback window: 30 calendar days after preview release publication, unless a later release decision replaces that policy.

Current Node `fgos setup` remains implemented as deprecated legacy compatibility and consumes the same registry while it exists.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
## 2. Registry Types

| Registry | Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check | `registerCheck` | A named diagnostic reported by `fgos doctor`. |
| Fix | `registerFix` | A named repair run by `fgos doctor --fix`; current legacy `fgos setup` also runs fixes while it remains implemented. |
| Config default | `registerConfigDefault` | A default config shape merged into shared config without overwriting user values. |

`event-store` registers the `eventStore` config shape `{ remote: "origin" }`. Config merge fills missing keys while preserving explicit remote choices; `git-publication-refspecs` diagnoses and repairs obsolete exact legacy mappings on the configured remote and on historical `origin`.

The registries are independent. A module may register only a check, only a fix, only a config default, or any combination.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.title: 3. Doctor Contract
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sample: 3. Doctor Contract
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.text: ## 3. Doctor Contract
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
## 3. Doctor Contract

`fgos doctor`:

- runs registered checks;
- reports individual pass/fail status;
- does not write files by default;
- should tell the user what command or fix path applies when a check fails.

Run coverage is checked by `observe-run-coverage`: the host's `metrics coverage`
must report layout rule `v2` and valid observed/skipped accounting. Doctor
independently compares both eligible unique results and candidate-directory/
barrier counts against the Node production admission projection and layout scan.
Both read the main checkout store, including from a worktree. A candidate run
directory changed in the last 60 seconds permits a bounded transient difference,
even before a result exists; future mtimes are recent for clock skew. The host's
`recentRuns` remains result-file based. Diagnostic paths are sample candidates,
not verified host omissions. An unknown coverage subcommand or a response
without `layoutRule` identifies an old host positively and reports
passed-but-degraded with an upgrade instruction; other host errors fail.
This check is read-only, introduces no config default, and never rewrites runs.

`convention-conformance` checks the packaged naming and placement rules only
inside an fgOS source checkout. Violations on paths already present at the
rule cutoff pass with counts and up to three examples; a violation on a path
introduced after that cutoff fails the check, even while the rule posture is
`warn`. A missing or old host pass-skips with the reason because doctor never
reimplements the native rules. The check is read-only and has no registered
fix or config default.


`active-release-matches-checkout` compares a source checkout's Node payload
working-tree bytes with its own activated manifest, using the release builder's
source enumeration. It reports changed, missing and extra source files, excludes
staged production dependencies, and does not certify Rust host freshness.
Outside source checkouts, without activation, with a same-checkout development
manifest, or in a linked worktree whose activation belongs to main, it reports
a reasoned skip. Unsafe paths and unreadable inputs fail this check rather than
throwing out the whole doctor run. It is read-only, with no registered fix:
`npm run fgos:dev -- <verb>` runs working-tree code; build/stage/upgrade updates
plain `fgos`. Diagnosis never changes the activation implicitly.


`fgos doctor --fix`:

- runs every registered fix;
- reports fix results;
- then reports checks.

New distribution design should route workspace onboarding through `fgctl init` plus local `fgos init`/`doctor --fix`/`doctor`, while preserving `fgos setup` as the legacy shell/global integration path through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces that behavior. The Git checks share one ABI/floor row, `git-component-compatible`. `git-operation-journal` reports pending count, oldest unresolved operation and retained bytes, and refuses unreadable or incomplete scans. Native locks are detected without removal. `git-wal-dir` initializes the trusted WAL directories; `git-driver-directories` creates or tightens only the current user’s designated fgOS root and empty driver hooks directory, canonicalizing a symlinked state root, rejecting symlinked hooks/foreign owners and leaving parents untouched; existing root chmod additionally requires canonical basename `fgos` or the driver’s own floor-record marker; Git doctor refusals name the mode/owner cause and this registered fix. `git-publication-refspecs` reads the canonical Git RepositoryConfig mapping for the effective `eventStore.remote` (project over global, default `origin`), installs missing wildcard mirror mappings and replaces the obsolete exact legacy line using RepositoryConfig under repo-config 80, preserving user configuration and recording the effective remote URL. `event-store` registers `eventStore.remote` with default `origin`; obsolete exact origin mappings are also repaired when a different remote is configured. Reserved legacy-suffix mirrors are reported for manual cleanup. A missing addon makes the checks fail and fixes report a refusal without aborting unrelated setup fixes. Durability reports the process-crash/fsync contract without certifying stable media.

`git-transport-config` reports repository-local transport settings that Publication/Remote refuse, using Rust’s scope-based admission policy. For actions/checkout credentials, use `persist-credentials: false`, remove the repo-local `http.<url>.extraheader`, and configure a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. The check is read-only, reports keys without credential values, and has no automatic credential migration.

Native locks are detected without removal. `git-wal-dir` initializes the trusted WAL directories; `git-driver-directories` creates or tightens only the current user’s designated fgOS root and empty driver hooks directory, canonicalizing a symlinked state root, rejecting symlinked hooks/foreign owners and leaving parents untouched; existing root chmod additionally requires canonical basename `fgos` or the driver’s own floor-record marker; Git doctor refusals name the mode/owner cause and this registered fix. `git-publication-refspecs` reads the canonical Git RepositoryConfig mapping for the effective `eventStore.remote` (project over global, default `origin`), installs missing wildcard mirror mappings and replaces the obsolete exact legacy line using RepositoryConfig under repo-config 80, preserving user configuration and recording the effective remote URL. `event-store` registers `eventStore.remote` with default `origin`; obsolete exact origin mappings are also repaired when a different remote is configured. Reserved legacy-suffix mirrors are reported for manual cleanup. A missing addon makes the checks fail and fixes report a refusal without aborting unrelated setup fixes. Durability reports the process-crash/fsync contract without certifying stable media.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.title: Contributor hooks setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sample: Contributor hooks setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.text: ##### Contributor hooks setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
##### Contributor hooks setup

- **Blocked when:** never — this is an explicit command a contributor runs
  themselves; it always runs when invoked.
- **What changes:** running the setup command wires up this repository's
  pre-commit hook for the person who just cloned it. It is never triggered
  automatically by any package manager's install step (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle)
  — a contributor runs it once, by hand, after cloning.
- **Side effects:** none beyond the local git config change; nothing is
  installed and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the contributor's local clone has the pre-commit hook
  wired up, identically to what used to happen automatically. Someone who
  never runs this command simply does not get the local hook — this is a
  one-time manual step for contributors, not a requirement for installing
  or running `fgos` itself.
- In fgOS source checkouts, the hook refuses newly staged root files outside
  its own allowlist, including linked worktrees and `fgw/*` branches. Existing
  root modifications/deletions remain permitted. Allowlist changes must land
  separately on main before root additions use them; the index cannot authorize
  itself. Merge commits skip only this root guard, never existing data-loss
  guards. `main-checkout-hook-wired` diagnoses wiring using the existing check.
- In fgOS source checkouts, the hook sends newly staged, copied, or renamed
  Markdown files directly under `plans/reports/` and `plans/journals/` to the
  native Convention checker. Violations and unavailable, old, or failed hosts
  emit warnings only; the hook never blocks the commit for Convention results.
  Nested evidence and per-plan `reports/` directories are outside this scope.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.title: Setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sample: Setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.text: ##### Setup
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
##### Setup

- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `lock` config section (`predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000`) is one of the
  defaults the fill-missing-only merge adds. Because setup runs every
  registered fix, it also attempts the `lock-fences` cutover step (row 7b),
  which places nothing unless the workspace's activated release already
  runs holder-lock and no other fgOS process of the workspace is running.
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), and the two lock
  directories may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.title: Doctor
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sample: Doctor
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.text: ##### Doctor
docs/platform/packaging-distribution/con.sectionText:
##### Doctor

- **Blocked when:** never — `fgos doctor` always runs every check and
  reports the result; it never fails the invocation itself, only reports
  individual checks as passing or not. Exit stays 0 because `fgctl
  init|upgrade|repair` run it as their tail and mark the install degraded on
  a non-zero exit; `--strict` is the opt-in that exits 1 when any check fails.
- **What changes:** nothing — this is a read-only diagnostic. It never
  writes a config file, never modifies a shell profile, and never installs
  anything, even when a check reports a problem (`config-not-stale`
  failing on a missing config file reports that plainly rather than
  creating one).
- **Side effects:** none.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees each named check (Data Dictionary #7) and
  whether it passed, including enough detail to know what to do next (e.g.
  which config settings are missing, or that `fgos setup` has not been run
  yet).

docs/platform/process/spec.md.sample: 1. Purpose
ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 1. Purpose
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 1. Purpose

The process component is the lowest layer (L0) under every lock, supervisor and gate. It owns two things and nothing else:

- **Facts.** `judge(tuple, observer) → alive | dead | unknown` for a normalized process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}`; the boot id, the start time and the pid namespace of a process; the list of processes holding a lock description; and the read-only scan the stop-everything cutover uses.
- **Control.** Spawning with an explicit fd mapping, signalling a process by identity (never by bare pid), and the two domain primitives the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs: is a domain empty, kill a whole domain.

Facts are almost never on the lock decision path any more (the kernel decides); they serve binding a supervisor or gate to its process, the temporary hot path, display, and the `linux-gate` domain. Control knows nothing about a run, an envelope, a lock or a pane.

| Owns | Does not own |

docs/platform/process/spec.md.title: 3. Facts: the judge table
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sample: 3. Facts: the judge table
ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 3. Facts: the judge table
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 3. Facts: the judge table

The tuple is `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}`. A record written before the tuple existed carries `processStartTime`; the adapter reads it as `startTime`. Rules are evaluated in order; the first that applies decides.

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| Other host, or other pid namespace without a decisive anchor | unknown |
| Same host, recorded boot id differs from the running kernel's | dead |
| No pid in the record (missing, corrupt, not a positive integer) | unknown (the Node leaf answered `dead` here before; a record without a pid proves nothing) |
| pid does not exist (`ESRCH`) | dead |
| pid exists in state `Z` or `X` in `/proc/<pid>/stat` | dead (`kill(pid, 0)` still succeeds for a zombie; the stat state decides) |
| pid exists, start time matches | alive |
| pid exists, start time differs (pid reused) | dead |
| Start time cannot be read (driver missing, permission, timeout) | unknown |

A process inside an attempt's PID namespace has no pid the host can read, and the reverse. The gate sets `FGOS_PIDNS_ANCHOR` (its own host tuple) for every process in the namespace; a record written inside carries `{pidNs, pid, startTime, anchor}`.

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| Record pid namespace differs from the observer's, the record has an anchor, and the anchor is dead | dead (when a namespace's init dies the kernel has killed the whole namespace) |
| Record pid namespace differs; anchor alive, unknown or absent | unknown: hold (never judge a holder you cannot see dead) |
| The observer is not in the initial PID namespace and the record has no `pidNs` (an old `{pid, startTime}` record) | unknown: hold (an agent in a sandbox running `fgos` must not clean a host holder's record) |

Consequence: a holder inside an attempt that dies while holding a hot lock keeps it until the attempt ends (bounded by the hard ceiling), never for ever; a process inside a namespace never steals a host process's lock.

Authoritative boot id: Linux `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`; macOS `sysctl kern.bootsessionuuid`; Windows has no boot id and uses the process creation time (`FILETIME`), which does not repeat when a pid is reused. Boot is never inferred from a clock minus uptime, and mtime is never used. The leaf reader never spawns: the macOS Node driver does not call `ps`, and a missing start time is `unknown`.

The same vectors are run by cargo and by the Node leaf, so there is no second judge table. `resolveHolderLiveness` in the Node leaf becomes an adapter of `judge` (`dead → 'dead'`, `alive | unknown → 'held'`); the one behaviour change is that a record without a pid now reads `held` and a zombie reads `dead`. `pidExists(pid)` (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, `EPERM` counts as existing) is the one helper the cutover phases use in place of every private `isPidAlive` copy, which they delete in the same commit.

docs/platform/process/spec.md.sample: 4. Control
ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 4. Control
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 4. Control

- **Signal by identity.** Linux: `pidfd_open`, check the start time, `pidfd_send_signal`, so there is no pid-reuse window. Other platforms: the tuple is checked right before `kill`, and the remaining window is stated.
- **Spawn with an explicit fd mapping.** `spawn_with_fds(cmd, fd_map)` closes every fd above 2 that is not in the map; a mapped fd is `dup2`'d in `pre_exec` and is not `CLOEXEC` only at that moment (holder-lock description rule 1). The leak test: a child spawned with `{3: fd}` has the inode at fd 3, a grandchild spawned without a map does not, and a child spawned with no map at all does not either.
- **Domain primitives.** `domain_is_empty(domain) → Empty | NotEmpty | Unknown` and `domain_kill_all(domain) → Ok | Refused`. In this track only `linux-gate` is implemented: empty iff `judge(tuple) == dead` (the kernel kills and reaps every task of the namespace before its init becomes a zombie), and `kill_all` is `signal_by_identity(tuple, SIGKILL)`. `windows-job` is judged by the Windows domain functions of `windows_job.rs`; `macos-tree` by the `macos-tree` containment driver (group plus descendant scan, with a second scan after 500 ms when judged from the record alone). Each answers `Unknown` and `Refused` on the other platforms.

Public types carry no raw fd or `pid_t`: `ProcId(u32)`, `FdSlot(u32)`, with `#[cfg(unix)]` inside the driver.

docs/platform/process/spec.md.title: 5. OS-neutral port
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sample: 5. OS-neutral port
ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 5. OS-neutral port
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 5. OS-neutral port

`ProcessPlatform` (facts + control) has one driver per OS. Linux is complete. macOS and Windows are real drivers for the parts that have clear semantics only: macOS reads the boot id through `sysctl`, reports `lock_holders` as `Unlistable` and `scan` as `Unsupported`; Windows uses the creation time in place of a boot id, `Unlistable`, `Unsupported`. `cargo check` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `aarch64-apple-darwin` is part of the crate's acceptance.

The containment port (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with the Linux `bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` drivers, the Windows `windows-job` driver and the macOS `macos-tree` driver is specified in section 10; the holder-lock track shipped only the two domain primitives above. Measured levels, for the record: Linux kernel (PID namespace when a user namespace is available, else best-effort process group), Windows kernel (Job Object, asynchronous kill, hence the predecessor rule), macOS best-effort (a `setsid` + double-fork escapee survives a group kill, measured on macOS 26.6).

ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 6. Quiescence scan
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 6. Quiescence scan

`scan(filter) → Vec<ProcView{tuple, exe, cmdline, cwd, env_subset}>` reads `/proc/*/{cmdline,cwd,environ}` on Linux. An entry that cannot be read (permission, vanished) is counted as `unreadable`, never skipped silently, because the stop-everything check must not report clean on a partial view. The route `fgos internal quiesce-scan` exposes it ([holder-lock spec, section 10](../holder-lock/spec.md#10-internal-routes)); on other platforms the answer is `unavailable` and a person confirms that no fgOS process is left.

docs/platform/process/spec.md.title: 7. Known limits
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sample: 7. Known limits
ancestry: Process Facts And Control Component Specification
docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 7. Known limits
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 7. Known limits

- A start time that cannot be read is `unknown`, so a holder whose `/proc` entry is hidden (another user, a hardened mount) is held, never cleaned.
- The macOS and Windows drivers cannot list lock holders; diagnostics there say `unlistable`.
- Without a user namespace the Linux containment level is best-effort; that is reported by the run supervisor's doctor check, not here.
- Two `/proc` readers remain outside this crate until their owners move: the Session Identity process-tree adapter and the Observe store lock reader.

docs/platform/process/spec.md.text: ## 8. Lịch sử quyết định
docs/platform/process/spec.md.sectionText:
## 8. Lịch sử quyết định

- **2026-10-15 — Thiết kế nền bản 3: facts rời khỏi đường quyết định lock.** Kernel lock quyết ai giữ; facts chỉ còn cho binding supervisor/gate, fast path nóng tạm thời và hiển thị. Tuple chuẩn `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}`; boot id từ nguồn có thẩm quyền, không từ đồng hồ, không mtime. [Design r6](../../../plans/reports/design-261016-1238-lock-and-run-supervisor-foundation-v3-r6.md) §5.1.
- **2026-10-16 — Phản biện vòng 1 (gemini R3-3): zombie và record thiếu pid.** `kill(pid, 0)` thành công với zombie nên zombie bị coi là sống; record thiếu pid bị `process-identity.mjs` coi là chết. Sửa: trạng thái `Z`/`X` → dead; thiếu pid → unknown (giữ). Design §14 vòng 1.
- **2026-10-16 — Phản biện vòng 2 (Argon R4-1) và vòng 3 (kongming N3, N4): PID namespace.** pid trong namespace không có nghĩa với host; gate đặt `FGOS_PIDNS_ANCHOR`, record trong namespace mang anchor; anchor chết → dead, còn lại → unknown; người phán ngoài init namespace gặp record không `pidNs` → unknown (agent trong sandbox không dọn record của holder host). "Miền rỗng" của attempt là `judge(gate) == dead`, quét inode namespace chỉ để chẩn đoán. Design §5.1, §14.
- **2026-10-16 — Plan 4.2 (Lead D3, D8): phạm vi của crate trong track này.** Không có primitive cho gate (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) vì 4.2 không có consumer; chỉ hai primitive miền `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` với `linux-gate` cài thật, `windows-job`/`macos-tree` trả `Unknown`/`Refused` tới khi driver tương ứng có. Leaf Node `process-identity.mjs` đọc cùng vector, `resolveHolderLiveness` thành adapter của `judge`, thêm `pidExists` để các phase cutover thay mọi bản chép `isPidAlive`. [Plan](../../../plans/261016-1104-holder-lock-kernel-lock-foundation/plan.md).
- **2026-10-19 — `arm_parent_death_signal` và đọc `/proc/locks` tới EOF.** Primitive PDEATHSIG cho gate terminal nằm ở crate này (gate gọi trước HELLO; run supervisor đóng cửa sổ monitor chết trước khi cài, xem [run-supervisor spec](../run-supervisor/spec.md) mục 16). `lock_table_entries` đọc hết một seq_file mở tới EOF thay vì một prefix: bảng không atomic, nên vắng mặt vẫn chỉ là lý do chạy probe shared-lock, không phải bằng chứng đã nhả.
