docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao BỀN, dừng CHỈ khi có tín hiệu tường minh — str7-str8-priority-intent).** `fgos-runner --watch` lặp lại nguyên vẹn vòng đời "Một vòng --once" nhiều lượt liên tiếp, KHÔNG dừng khi frontier rỗng (khác `--once`, vốn dừng khi rỗng): một lượt vừa GHI được gì (bất kỳ giao dịch cửa-ghi nào thành công) thì lượt kế tiếp bắt đầu NGAY, không chờ; một lượt không ghi được gì thì lượt kế tiếp chờ một khoảng nghỉ mặc định (đổi được qua `--poll-ms`) trước khi thử lại. Bộ đếm cầu dao (Data Dictionary #5) dùng CHUNG một thực thể xuyên suốt MỌI lượt của một tiến trình `--watch` — khác `--once`, nơi mỗi lời gọi có cầu dao riêng — nên cầu dao KHÔNG còn trơ dưới `--watch`: một việc lỗi rải rác qua nhiều lượt vẫn cộng dồn tới trần, đúng ý nghĩa "tiến trình bền tích lũy lịch sử lỗi" của chế độ này. Một lượt gặp lỗi/dừng (halted) KHÔNG kết thúc tiến trình `--watch` — chỉ lượt đó dừng, tiến trình vẫn tiếp tục thử lượt kế tiếp; DUY NHẤT tín hiệu dừng tường minh (SIGINT/SIGTERM) kết thúc tiến trình, luôn thoát mã 0 bất kể lượt cuối cùng ra sao. Một tín hiệu dừng thứ hai (người gõ Ctrl-C lần nữa khi lượt đang chạy còn dở) buộc thoát ngay (mã 130) — lối thoát khẩn cho một lượt kẹt, không chờ nó tự xong. `--watch` không tương thích với `--dry-run` (bị chặn `validation`); `--watch --once` không lỗi — `--watch` mặc nhiên thắng, giữ đúng tiền lệ `--once` đã là cờ chấp-nhận-nhưng-không-đọc (per str7-str8-priority-intent).

docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb — per D2 str46-io-contract).** Mỗi lượt `--once`, và mỗi chu kỳ của `--watch`, in đúng MỘT phong bì `fgos.v1` (cùng bốn trường `contract`/`generated_at`/`data_hash`/`data` đã tả ở spec Work-State "Phong bì output") thay cho dòng chữ trần trước đây — nhưng in **liền một dòng**, không xuống dòng nhiều tầng như `fgos.mjs`: một tiến trình `--watch` sống lâu phát NHIỀU phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian, nên mỗi phong bì phải trọn trong đúng một dòng để bên đọc tách được cái này với cái kia. Với `--once`, phong bì này luôn là dòng cuối cùng của kết quả. **Ba luồng output khác của `fgos-runner` KHÔNG đổi, nằm ngoài phong bì này có chủ đích:** (1) tiến trình dò-xét từng bước bên trong một lượt (gặt-lại, nhận việc, phán làm-rõ/chia-việc, đuôi kết quả proof, thử lại, dừng) tiếp tục in thẳng ra console y nguyên như trước — luồng này thuộc "Ghi lại output của trợ lý sau mỗi lượt dispatch"/"Xem live output worker khi đang chạy" đã tả trên, một tính năng tách bạch không đụng tới; (2) bản ghi cục bộ mỗi việc (`.fgos/logs/<id>.log`) không đổi; (3) dòng xác nhận đã dừng khi nhận tín hiệu dừng tường minh (RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao bền, dừng chỉ khi có tín hiệu tường minh)) vẫn là chữ trần, không bọc phong bì — đây là một dòng vòng-đời-tiến-trình, không phải kết cục của một lượt việc. Vì hai luồng (phong bì kết cục + dò-xét từng bước) độc lập và cùng ra `stdout`, bên đọc PHẢI phân biệt phong bì thật bằng cách phân tích một dòng thành JSON rồi kiểm `contract === 'fgos.v1'` — KHÔNG BAO GIỜ bằng cách đoán qua dấu hiệu chữ (vd "dòng bắt đầu bằng `{`"), vì dòng dò-xét từng bước có thể tự nhiên chứa `{` (proof của việc tự in JSON).

docs/specs/runner.md.text:
- **RUL63 (`executors.<id>.allowCrossProvider` — cổng governance chặn nội dung prompt rời hệ Claude qua 1 backend không rõ nguồn, mặc định hạn chế; phạm vi mở rộng thành kind-độc-lập, tsk-in1-4 D5).** `resolveExecutorConfig` (`src/runner/dispatch.mjs`), sau khi giải executor thắng cuộc theo thứ tự ưu tiên `executors.<executorId>` > `executor` (tsk-62v; rung trung gian `executors.<tier>` đã rút, tsk-in1-2), kiểm thêm: nếu `command` CUỐI CÙNG đã giải KHÔNG nằm trong danh sách CLI-Claude đã biết (`CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS`, hiện chỉ `'claude'` — cố ý KHÔNG dùng chung `KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES`, vì danh sách đó có `'codex'`, một CLI không phải Claude) VÀ executor không mang `allowCrossProvider: true` tường minh → ném `RunnerConfigError` ngay tại thời điểm resolve, TRƯỚC bất kỳ dispatch nào — không bao giờ âm thầm gửi nội dung ra backend khác. Phép kiểm dựa trên `command` CUỐI CÙNG đã giải (không phải `kind` khai báo đơn thuần, không phải `provider` — nhãn hiển thị tự khai tùy ý, có thể spoof). Miễn trừ DUY NHẤT: một executor giải qua `buildAgentTypeExecutor` (không tự khai `command`/`adapter`/`invocations` — chỉ `agentType`) luôn tái dùng `command` của `executor` toàn cục, trên thực tế luôn là Claude, nên phép kiểm này tự vô hiệu cho đường đó — KHÔNG phải một miễn trừ theo `kind`. Trước tsk-in1-4, phạm vi CHỈ áp dụng cho `kind: "cli"` (`kind: "task"` được miễn trừ thẳng theo khai báo — lỗ hổng thật: 1 executor `kind:"task"` không có `agentType`, rơi thẳng về `executor` toàn cục qua đường KHÁC `buildAgentTypeExecutor`, đáng lẽ vẫn cần kiểm nếu `executor` đó không phải Claude, nhưng được bỏ qua nhầm). tách `kind` khỏi vai trò "cờ miễn trừ" — `agy` (`kind:"agent"`) VẪN cần `allowCrossProvider` cho backend `agy` CLI không phải Claude của nó, y hệt trước. Vắng mặt hoặc `false` ở `allowCrossProvider` luôn nghĩa là CHẶN (mặc định hạn chế) — không bao giờ đọc ngược thành "cho phép trừ khi đánh dấu nhạy cảm" (per - tsk-32n, xem `docs/history/capacity-cross-provider-governance/CONTEXT.md`+`plan.md`).
- **RUL65 (`executors.<id>.kind` là `agent`/`tool` — trục BẢN CHẤT, tách khỏi `invocations[].via` — trục CƠ CHẾ GỌI; tsk-in1-4 D5/D8/D9).** Trước item này, `kind` gánh 2 vai đồng thời: mượn thẳng `tool-registry.mjs`'s `KINDS` (`cli`/`binary`/`mcp`/`skill`) làm cơ chế probe-presence CHO CẢ dispatch, cộng thêm `'task'` cho dispatch native — 1 field, 2 câu hỏi khác nhau ("đây LÀ gì" và "gọi NÓ bằng cách nào"), khiến `gitnexus`'s `kind:"mcp"` và `herdr`'s `kind:"cli"` phải mang nghĩa kép không liên quan. Từ tsk-in1-4: `EXECUTOR_KINDS = ['agent', 'tool']` — `agent` = 1 persona sống, có thể dispatch-native khi phiên gọi có live Task access (`decideExecutorDispatchMechanism` đọc `kind === 'agent'`, không còn `'task'`); `tool` = cơ học, presence-only theo thiết kế gốc (`gitnexus`/`herdr`), dù về mặt cơ chế 1 entry `kind:"tool"` khai `command`/`args` phẳng vẫn dispatch được qua `resolveExecutorConfig` bình thường — `kind` chỉ quyết định tính đủ-điều-kiện-native, không phải có-dispatch-được-hay-không. Cơ chế gọi dời hẳn sang `invocations[].via` — `INVOCATION_VIA = ['cli', 'task', 'mcp']` (`'binary'`/`'skill'`/`'http'` bỏ khi gộp từ vocab cũ của `tool-registry.mjs`, `'api'` chưa quay lại — 0 producer lịch sử, bằng chứng qua `.fgos/events.jsonl`). `tool-registry.mjs`'s `toolsFromExecutors` (`src/state/tool-registry.mjs`) đọc probe-kind/probe-command từ `invocations[0].via`/`.command`, không còn từ `executor.kind` nữa — hệ quả trực tiếp của việc tách trục.

docs/specs/runner.md.sample: - **RUL65b (Provider Capacity Rotator slice 1 — account selection là runtime capacity, không phải placement/fallback).** Khi một Assignment Run đã qua admission và executor thắng c
docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL65b (Provider Capacity Rotator slice 1 — account selection là runtime capacity, không phải placement/fallback).** Khi một Assignment Run đã qua admission và executor thắng cuộc là `kind:"agent"` out-of-process cho provider có inventory global (slice 1: `openai-codex`), runner acquire đúng một account lease dưới lock global trước launch; `dispatch-plan.json` chỉ ghi requirement, không bao giờ ghi selected account trước admission. Ranking cố định: `openLeases` tăng dần, rồi `lastSelectedAt` tăng dần, rồi `stableHash(seed, accountId)`; sticky assignment chỉ được giữ nếu account vẫn present, healthy, non-quarantined. Lease sống theo Run lifetime và chỉ reclaim khi có proof PID-dead/run-dead, không bao giờ vì elapsed TTL. `kind:"tool"`/MCP executors (ví dụ GitNexus) bypass rotator bằng discriminator hiện hữu, dù cùng provider label.

docs/specs/runner.md.sample: Selection evidence là Run-owned (`provider-capacity-selection.json`, effective execution contract/evidence) và chỉ được persist dạng redacted: provider, account id/label, lease own
docs/specs/runner.md.text: Selection evidence là Run-owned (`provider-capacity-selection.json`, effective execution contract/evidence) và chỉ được persist dạng redacted: provider, account id/label, lease owner, reason codes/quarantine state, `credentialProvisioned`; không persist credential home path, env values, token, `auth.json` bytes, raw digest/SHA-256. Provisioning của invocation bwrap (cli-spawn và herdr-spawn) dùng selected account `credentialSource` để copy vào private home trước spawn — kind `codex-home` copy `auth.json` vào private `CODEX_HOME`, kind `home-files` (`files`: danh sách đường dẫn tương đối, không `..`) copy đúng các file đó vào private home của agent khác (pi, agy), owner-only, giữ exec bit của helper; inventory vẫn chỉ ở `~/.fgos/config.json`, và pane herdr confine dựa vào nó để khởi động đã đăng nhập (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §13.1, doctor `confined-pane-accounts`); mất/không đọc/copy lỗi thì fail closed trước spawn với class credential-provisioning/config, không quarantine account, không bind-mount real Codex home, và không còn dùng `FGOS_CODEX_CREDENTIAL_HOMES` hash rotation hay executor-id allowlist làm authority placement.

docs/specs/runner.md.title: Unheaded block 72
docs/specs/runner.md.sample: Fault classifier chỉ đọc high-confidence provider stderr, adapter outcome đã biết (`paused-limit`), hoặc structured agent JSON như `stopReason`; không scan prompt/brief/report/gene
docs/specs/runner.md.text: Fault classifier chỉ đọc high-confidence provider stderr, adapter outcome đã biết (`paused-limit`), hoặc structured agent JSON như `stopReason`; không scan prompt/brief/report/general stdout. Quota/rate-limit quarantine account; auth/login/token quarantine dạng manual-clear; credential provisioning/config/test/confinement/work-product failure không quarantine. Chủ máy đặt quarantine tay bằng `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --until <ISO tương lai> --reason "<why>"` (quota-limit tạm thời, `detail.kind: owner`; unknown account hoặc `--until` không ở tương lai bị refuse; ghi vào state thật của máy, không theo `--dir`). Classifier cũng đọc giờ reset tuyệt đối codex in ("try again at 6:02 PM", giờ local, lần kế tiếp). Manual clear duy nhất là `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --reason "<why>"` (unknown provider/account bị refuse; non-quarantined account bị refuse trừ khi `--force`). `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` và `fgos doctor` chỉ report; doctor không auto-clear auth quarantine. `readOnlyExecutorRedirects` vẫn giữ nguyên trong slice này; không có `providerFallback`, `providerRuntimes`, `providers.<provider>.models`, six-tier runtime wiring, cross-provider fallback, hay retry loop trong rotator.

docs/specs/runner.md.title: Unheaded block 73
docs/specs/runner.md.sample: Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocatio
docs/specs/runner.md.text: Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocation under a fresh `-fb<n>` assignment id while another account of that candidate's pool is usable (listed in the inventory, enabled, not quarantined) and fewer retries than that pool has accounts were spent on this candidate; the lease then takes the next account in the order the config declares (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool)). Only when no account is left does `nextCandidate` walk the tier's candidates (the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.<tier>` declares), skipping pools whose login failed in this unit and still preferring a family the sibling seats did not use. A process that exits non-zero with a dead-credential wording (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, e.g. pi "No API key found for openrouter.") in its last five stderr lines settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: credential`, so the account is quarantined as `auth-token`. A process that exits the same way with a used-up quota as its last words (`QUOTA_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `provider-auth-failure.mjs`, line-start anchored after an optional `ERROR:`; measured: codex "ERROR: You’ve hit your usage limit. ... try again at 11:39 PM.", 2026-10-13) settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota`, with or without an account lease, so a headless cli-spawn round rotates and walks like a pane round; a leased account is quarantined `quota-limit` until the reset the provider printed (the existing `until`, no separate retry field), and a quota stop does not exclude the provider family. The capacity classifier reads the same wordings from the stderr tail only. Rescheduling a run whose accounts and candidates are all used up is not done here (Workflow runner, separate decision). Each attempt records `fallbackFrom.kind` (`account-rotation` or `next-candidate`).

docs/specs/runner.md.text:
Đi kèm bắt buộc 3 gate, thiếu 1 trong 3 thì `gitnexus` (chỉ có `invocations:[{via:"mcp",...}]`, không `command`/`args` phẳng) vỡ ngay lúc load hoặc bị spawn nhầm:
  - **Gate B1 (shape-theo-via, `validateInvocationShape`).** Không ép hình dạng executor (`command` string + `args` array) lên MỌI invocation bất kể `via` — `via:"cli"` cần đủ hình dạng executor thật (sẽ spawn thật); `via:"mcp"` chỉ cần `command` là 1 định danh không rỗng (không bao giờ spawn, không cần `args`); `via:"task"` không cần cả hai (dispatch native không mang subprocess argv).
  - **Gate B2 (chọn đúng invocation theo `via`, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Không lấy `invocations[0]` mù — chọn ĐÚNG entry có `via:"cli"` (cơ chế DUY NHẤT `resolveExecutorConfig` thật sự dispatch), bất kể thứ tự khai trong mảng.
 - **Gate B3 (throw tường minh khi không dispatch-được, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Khi 1 executor khai `invocations` nhưng KHÔNG entry nào `via:"cli"` (như `gitnexus`) — ném `RunnerConfigError` ngay, không bao giờ âm thầm rơi về `executor` toàn cục như thể executor đó chỉ mang metadata (khác hẳn 1 executor thật sự không khai `invocations`/`command`/`adapter`/`agentType` nào — ca đó vẫn rơi về `executor` toàn cục bình thường).

docs/specs/runner.md.text: **Trạng thái triển khai (tsk-in1-4):** code + test (fixture tổng hợp) đã xong và xanh; `.fgos/config.json` SỐNG của chính repo này CHƯA migrate (`agy.kind` vẫn `"cli"`, `gitnexus`/`herdr` vẫn hình dạng cũ) — khác `runner.capabilities` (RUL trên, tsk-in1-3, thuần cộng thêm nên nạp được ở cả code cũ lẫn mới), đổi `kind` là đổi PHÁ VỠ tương thích ngược: code cũ từ chối thẳng `kind:"agent"/"tool"`. Nên KHÔNG commit thẳng lên `main` như các item liền trước (ADR0020 (chặn .fgos/ khỏi worktree worker — fgw/<id> không symlink lẫn bootstrap-copy .fgos/, merge.mjs từ chối cứng diff chạm .fgos/)'s "commit trực tiếp lên main, tách khỏi vòng đời code" chỉ an toàn khi dữ liệu mới còn tương thích code cũ) — phải land ĐỒNG THỜI với code của `fgw/tsk-in1` khi nhánh đó được merge lên `main`, không phải trước.

docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL66 (`EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS`' chữ ký tổng quát hoá thành `(invocation, opts)`; `'api'` quay lại `INVOCATION_VIA` với 1 adapter `http` thật; tsk-in1-5).** Trước item này `EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS` map tên adapter → hàm `(command, args, cwd, opts)` — 1 hình dạng định hình sẵn theo CLI argv, đúng "bẫy B1" (tsk-in1-4's gate B1 đã đóng cho `validateInvocationShape`, nhưng port thực thi bên dưới vẫn ép mọi adapter vào khuôn CLI). Từ tsk-in1-5: mỗi adapter nhận thẳng `(invocation, opts)` — `invocation` là bất cứ hình dạng nào adapter đó cần (`cliSpawnAdapter` đọc `command`/`args`; `httpAdapter` đọc `method`/`url`/`headers`/`body`), `opts` giữ nguyên field chung không phụ thuộc invocation (`cwd`, `timeoutMs`, `maxBuffer`, `onChunk`, `workId`, `tier`, `model` — `cwd` dời từ tham số riêng vào `opts` vì nó là ngữ cảnh thực thi, không phải dữ liệu invocation). `EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS` giờ đăng ký 2 adapter thật: `cli-spawn` (không đổi hành vi, chỉ đổi cách nhận tham số) và `http` (`httpAdapter`, tiền lệ pluggable THẬT — gọi HTTP thật qua `fetch`, timeout qua `AbortController` ném `DispatchError('worker-timeout',...)`, lỗi mạng ném `DispatchError('worker-spawn-fail',...)`, còn HTTP status khác 2xx KHÔNG bị coi là lỗi — cùng triết lý "exit code khác 0 không phải lỗi" áp cho `cli-spawn`). `INVOCATION_VIA` thêm lại `'api'` (từng bỏ vì 0 producer lịch sử — giờ có adapter thật đứng sau nên khôi phục: `['cli', 'task', 'mcp', 'api']`); Gate B1 (`validateInvocationShape`) thêm nhánh `via:"api"` yêu cầu `url` là string không rỗng, không ép `command`/`args`.

docs/specs/runner.md.text: **Phạm vi CHƯA làm (cố ý, đúng "tiền lệ" chứ không phải "tích hợp đầy đủ"):** `resolveExecutorConfig`'s gate B2/B3 (tsk-in1-4) VẪN chỉ chọn/spawn `via:"cli"` — chưa mở rộng để tự động dispatch 1 executor khai `via:"api"` qua `spawnWorker`/`executeExecutorCli`'s đường sản xuất thật. `httpAdapter` được test độc lập (gọi `EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS.http` trực tiếp với 1 test server local thật), không cần 1 executor thật đăng ký `via:"api"` — đúng như `agy` từng chứng minh `cli-spawn` trước khi có executor thứ hai nào dùng nó. Mỗi chokepoint dispatch thật (nơi 1 executor thật sự được thực thi hoặc quyết định hand-back native, không phải nơi chỉ resolve/quyết định suông) giờ in đúng 1 dòng `stderr` ngay trước khi dispatch xảy ra: `fgos: dispatch capability=<...> executor=<...> via=<...> provider=<...> model=<...> tier=<...>`.
 - `spawnWorker` (runner tự dispatch 1 work item): `capability` in ra là kết quả `executorIdForWork` (tên skill executing-stage theo domain/stage — TRỤC KHÁC hẳn danh mục `runner.capabilities`) vì đường này không đi qua `for`/`capabilities` catalog; nhãn dùng `job=` thay vì `capability=` ngay trong dòng in để tránh lẫn 2 khái niệm. `executor` in `(global executor)` khi `cfg.executors` không có entry khớp `executorIdForWork`'s kết quả ('s "miss cố ý").
  - `executeExecutorCli` nhánh in-process (`mechanism:"in-process"`, hand-back cho caller, KHÔNG tự spawn): dòng in thêm `agentType=<...>`, `provider`/`model`/`tier` đều `n/a` (chưa resolve tới bước đó).
  - `executeExecutorCli` nhánh out-of-process (tự spawn thật): dòng in đầy đủ `provider`/`model`/`tier` như thật sẽ dùng để spawn — in NGAY TRƯỚC lệnh `adapterFn(...)` thật, không phải sau.
  - `capability` (2 nhánh `executeExecutorCli`) ưu tiên `purpose` (flag `--for` caller truyền vào) khi có; không thì đọc `cfg.executors.<id>.for` của chính executor đó (nhiều giá trị nối bằng dấu phẩy) làm nhãn thông tin; rỗng thì in `(none declared)`.
  - Thuần diagnostic (`process.stderr.write`) — không phải phần giá trị trả về của bất kỳ hàm nào, không ai đọc lại nó; không đổi hành vi/return-value hiện có của `spawnWorker`/`executeExecutorCli`.

  Thay thế RUL69 (vocab modelTier 6 mức thay 5 mức cũ) về cơ chế map model và chuẩn hoá từ vựng toàn repo:
  1. Bên cầu (việc cần gì): từ duy nhất là `rigor = low | standard | high | critical` (thay thế `minTier`, `minRigor`, `mode`). `rigor` gộp chỉ-nâng qua các scope (Workflow/Unit → Operation → Actor → Assignment → CLI), rồi gộp sàn theo loại việc `capabilities.<cap>.rigor`.
  2. Bên cung (khẩu vị owner): ánh xạ qua đúng một bảng config bắt buộc `runner.rigorToTier[rigor] → tier` (`nano|mini|standard|advanced|flagship|frontier`), sau đó chọn model tại `runner.modelPolicies[provider][tier]`.
  3. Override tường minh: `--tier` / `actors[].tier` là kênh placement tường minh (chỉ-nâng, có provenance `tierSource`); definition/operation dùng `tier` bị từ chối.
  4. Work: tách `work.tier` thành `work.size` (độ lớn, không bao giờ tới model) và `work.rigor` (tuỳ chọn, discovery phán). Item cũ có `risk: heavy` và chưa có `rigor` được đọc thành `rigor: high` ở đường đọc duy nhất.
  5. Sàn theo loại việc `capabilities.<cap>.rigor` là sàn duy nhất theo loại việc, có hiệu lực ở cả đường coordination lẫn Work. Khối `capabilities.*.overrides` bị xoá hoàn toàn.
  6. Xoá vĩnh viễn không lặp lại: `minTier`, `minRigor`, `QUALITY_TIER_BRIDGE`, `QUALITY_MODE_VALUES`, `DEFAULT_TIER_TO_POLICY`, `rigorOverrides`, `runner.models`, `capabilities.*.overrides`. Test guard tự động chặn chúng quay lại.

- **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `src/state/**`, `src/workflow/**` hay bất kỳ module tầng Work (`work-compat`, `work-dispatch`, `operation-choice`, `loop`, `claim-port`, `prompt-templates`, `intake/`, `verbs/`), và không chứa literal tên domain/bước (guard `test/architecture.test.mjs`, tên đọc từ `domains/*/` trên đĩa). Cụ thể:
  1. Operation/taskSpec/skill của một bước đến từ định nghĩa Workflow (`domains/<d>/workflows/*.yaml`, `steps[].operations`/`skill`), tầng Work đọc qua `src/state/domain-registry.mjs` rồi đưa vào `buildAssignment({ domain, stage, operation, operations })`. Dispatch kiểm `operation ∈ operations` (lỗi `unknown operation ... for stage ...`), ghi danh sách hợp lệ vào `provenance.declared.legalOperations`; `executeAssignment` từ chối một Assignment declared không mang danh sách đó hoặc có `operation` ngoài danh sách (và `dispatch: human-only`). Trường `stage` trên Assignment hiện chỉ còn là nhãn mờ của bước (đổi tên theo đợt thuật ngữ).
  2. [Phần đầu vào còn lại ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only) — `work`/`workItem`/`workExecutorId` thôi là đầu vào của dispatch; `decide --work` nhận hint; `workDispatchContext` không còn trả `work`] Mọi thứ Work-aware chuyển ra tầng Work: `src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` (chọn operation cho bước hiện tại, trước ở `dispatch/`), `src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs` (`spawnWorker`, `resolveAgentTypeForWork`, `resolveWorkForDispatch`, `workDispatchContext`), `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (`executorIdForWork`, `buildPrompt`, `workCapabilityHints`). docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds).** An account quarantined as `auth-token` has no end time: the owner logs in again by hand and fgOS cannot see it. Instead of waiting for a person to run the clear command, a dispatch that finds **no usable account of the provider** makes one real, cheap call per such account (Codex: `codex exec`; an omp profile, a `home-files` source that lists `agent.db`: `omp -p`; a pi account directory, one that lists `auth.json`: `pi -p`; omp is tested before pi), against the account's own home, not a copy, because the owner uses that home and a renewal belongs there. A call that answers clears the lock (audited as `fgos provider-capacity probe`) and the dispatch goes on; one that does not keeps the lock and records the attempt, and no new call is made for that account within a 30 minute cooldown, however many dispatches ask. Only `auth-token` locks are probed: a quota limit ends by itself and any other manual lock is a person's decision. The call is never made while another account of the provider is usable, runs outside the state lock but inside the account lock of RUL75 (so a renewal made by fgOS cannot overlap it; an account whose lock stays busy past two minutes counts as a failed attempt), stops at the first account that answers, and a failure to probe never blocks the dispatch. A credential layout fgOS cannot name (the agy homes of Gemini) has no call, so that account stays locked for a person. The probe is passed to the dispatch by its callers; a caller that passes none changes nothing.

Opt-in (the same shape as the lazy probe): a caller passes `providerCredentialRenew` (`createCredentialRenewal()`, `src/runner/dispatch/provider-credential-renewal.mjs`) to `executeAssignment`, and only then do the two halves below run; without it provisioning and removal are as before. `agent.db` is copied as a consistent SQLite snapshot (`VACUUM INTO`, write-ahead log included) whether or not a dispatch opted in, and the unlock probe knows the omp layout regardless.

docs/specs/runner.md.text: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "executor phải khai capability" đã bỏ]; partly reverses the `execute --for` retirement of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch; `execute --for` đã rút), 2026-10-13).** `execute <id>` with no purpose infers the capability from the executor's own `for` list, a required-confinement capability first (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`). RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.

docs/specs/runner.md.sample: - **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the
docs/specs/runner.md.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
